description: sali-folio reference catalog for semantic ontology alignment. Generated from OWL source files on 2026-04-05. Source: LMSS.owl.

actions.reuse: The source concept maps directly to an existing type. Use the target type as-is.
actions.extend: The source concept requires a new type that inherits from a target base type via rdfs:subClassOf.

typePatterns.defined_class: Classes with necessary and sufficient conditions (owl:equivalentClass). Gives higher confidence in semantic coverage.
typePatterns.primitive_class: Classes with only necessary conditions (rdfs:subClassOf). The most common pattern.
typePatterns.restriction: Classes defined by property restrictions (someValuesFrom, allValuesFrom, cardinality).
typePatterns.union_class: Classes defined as the union of other classes.
typePatterns.intersection_class: Classes defined as the intersection of other classes.

properties.name: R1L3IueMeHCrxnDlOU2dRg
properties.label: sali:opposed
properties.definition: In the context of an argument, "opposed" refers to the stance taken against a particular claim, assertion, or position. An opposed argument counters or refutes the original claim by presenting contrary evidence, reasoning, or viewpoints. In debates or discussions, this oppositional stance is vital for ensuring a comprehensive exploration of the topic at hand.

properties.name: R1us3pQhG9zkEb39dZHByB
properties.label: sali:observed
properties.definition: In various legal contexts, "observed" refers to the act of witnessing, watching, or monitoring an event, situation, or process. This can include an attorney attending a deposition to oversee the process, a witness visually witnessing a crime, or a citizen attending and watching a trial. Observation in legal contexts can imply going beyond passive viewing, where the observer may potentially provide future testimony or use the observed information in later proceedings.

properties.name: R3DWdkCuByi2y5EimZYMab
properties.label: sali:owned
properties.definition: In legal and financial contexts, "owned" refers to the possession or holding of rights, titles, or interests in property, assets, or securities. This implies a legal relationship between the owner and the object of ownership, conferring certain rights, such as usage, control, and transfer. Ownership can apply to tangible assets like houses or intangible assets like shares in a company.

properties.name: R3FCcrFyaoiMddiRqdTfgf
properties.label: sali:not
properties.definition: A logical negation operator that excludes items containing the subsequent search term from the results.

properties.name: R3zM4v3AKS03zKslpmcdLP
properties.label: sali:analyzed
properties.definition: "Analyzed" in a legal context encompasses a comprehensive and methodical examination of legal issues, documents, or evidence. It involves applying critical thinking, legal knowledge, and analytical skills to understand, interpret, and draw conclusions from legal materials, often forming the basis for legal strategies, arguments, or decisions.

properties.name: R4HVaajKP29IEU6HxKgCBL
properties.label: sali:maxResults
properties.definition: Specifies a limit on the number of results returned by a query.

properties.name: R55RwIpe6K1xGWsaee45Ch
properties.label: sali:negotiated
properties.definition: In legal and business contexts, "negotiated" refers to the process of discussing, deliberating, and reaching an agreement or compromise between parties. This involves the back-and-forth exchange of proposals and concessions, with the goal of resolving differences and concluding an arrangement, such as a contract, settlement, or plea deal.

properties.name: R6qohvM786wjw0MNQJg9Dq
properties.label: sali:drafted
properties.definition: In the context of legal work, "drafted" refers to the process of composing and preparing legal documents, such as contracts, memos, pleadings, briefs, motions, or judicial opinions. This often involves a preliminary version subject to review, revision, and finalization.

properties.name: R74zuvPdysbm8JDf0v5JU4n
properties.label: sali:docketed
properties.definition: In legal procedures, "docketed" refers to the act of formally recording an document (e.g., application, motion) or proceeding (e.g., case, appeal, license proceeding), or other legal matter in the official registry or list of a government agency or court. This signifies that the matter has been officially entered into the system and is scheduled for consideration. A document may be "filed" but not "docketed," often because the clerk of court rejected the filing.

properties.name: R78CKihZmI99oRGDBSO0X9Z
properties.label: sali:reversed
properties.definition: In the legal domain, "reversed" refers to the decision of an appellate court to overturn or change the ruling of a lower court. This action indicates that the appellate court found errors or issues in the lower court's judgment that significantly affected the outcome, warranting a different legal conclusion.

properties.name: R7AjiNe4tLDt1Z4s1rZep1Y
properties.label: sali:accepted
properties.definition: In legal terms, "accepted" refers to the formal acknowledgment and approval of legal documents, filings, or propositions by a decisionmaker, court, judge, or other legal authority. This acceptance signifies that the material or argument meets required standards or criteria and is deemed suitable for consideration within the legal process.

properties.name: R7IaFnjI5OndDVqgzfMPpco
properties.label: sali:authored
properties.definition: In a legal context, "authored" refers to the creation or writing of a legal document, article, opinion, or other written work. In contrast with someone who "drafted" the document (and might be unnamed in the final document), persons who "authored" a document are named authors.

properties.name: R7Icq7RNxBnj6SSAqy0jvVa
properties.label: sali:equal
properties.definition: An operator that returns items where the field's value exactly matches the given value.

properties.name: R7N2b7y7ob6CHZK4mV5FO8R
properties.label: sali:billedTo
properties.definition: In the context of law and commerce, "billed to" refers to the process of issuing a bill or invoice by a service provider, seller, or vendor to a client, customer, or purchaser for goods sold or services rendered. This action signifies a request for payment, detailing the cost of services or products provided.

properties.name: R7NbWQfdIKgNd43XLIu6RHe
properties.label: sali:received
properties.definition: In various contexts, "received" denotes the act of being given or awarded something, such as a degree, license, or parole. This implies that the recipient has met certain criteria or conditions and has been formally granted a particular item, status, or privilege by an authoritative body or institution.

properties.definition: a collection of Roles

properties.name: R7VtpAC807aOYLVtKmPvFRt
properties.label: sali:argued
properties.definition: In a legal setting, "argued" refers to the presentation and advocacy of a legal position or interpretation before a court or tribunal. This process involves a structured discourse, utilizing facts, evidence, and legal principles to persuade the judge or jury of the validity of a party's stance or viewpoint on the matter at hand.

properties.name: R7rbNCX8S7kZnvn6AJc71MV
properties.label: sali:served
properties.definition: The act of legally serving something (e.g., a document) upon another entity. Example: Serving a Complaint upon a Defendant.

properties.name: R7s5qg2JvWQEFUPaLJSfUsf
properties.label: sali:negotiatedWith
properties.definition: In legal and business interactions, "negotiated with" refers to the act of engaging in discussions and bargaining with a specific party or entity to reach an agreement or resolve a dispute. This term highlights the relational aspect of negotiation, indicating a two-way process involving proposals, counter-proposals, and concessions between distinct parties, such as attorneys, individuals, organizations, or business entities.

properties.name: R7xbqZhraT1X45xH64uGCnw
properties.label: sali:isIssuedTo
properties.definition: In legal and administrative contexts, "issued to" refers to the formal granting or providing of a legal status, document, or financial instrument by an authoritative body or entity to a specific recipient. This term indicates that the recipient is the designated holder or beneficiary of the issued item, such as asylum status, a business license, or stock ownership.

properties.name: R84mzUh0Z3D44MrLDu0YAMw
properties.label: for expression
properties.definition: a LegalRuleML expression for which the Role is responsible (e.g., the expression was created or endorsed by the role).

properties.name: R84xWqLwURw9paxfFdpMlPY
properties.label: sali:isMostRecent
properties.definition: "Is Most Recent" in legal and administrative contexts refers to the latest version or update of a document, agreement, or legal ruling. This term indicates that the specified item has undergone revisions or updates and that this version supersedes all previous iterations, containing the most current information or terms.

properties.name: R86VduVUHypjaeAGBoLfXFB
properties.label: sali:renewed
properties.definition: "Renewed" refers to the act of extending the validity or duration of an existing agreement, license, or document. This process involves meeting the necessary requirements to continue the legal status, privileges, or rights originally granted, such as extending a visa, license, or lease term.

properties.name: R87URpvCOv2mK8a5Ivhm5qP
properties.label: sali:developStrategy
properties.definition: In the legal field, "develop strategy" refers to the process of creating a planned approach or method to achieve specific objectives in various legal contexts, such as contract negotiations or court hearings. This involves analyzing facts, anticipating challenges, and devising tactics to effectively represent a client's interests or achieve desired outcomes.

properties.name: R8CE2qvP7a4lK7h1khGxQk3
properties.label: sali:waitingFor
properties.definition: "Waiting for" is the state of anticipating or expecting a subsequent action, response, or document from another party. In legal proceedings and project management, this term often describes a period of inactivity where one party is dependent on the completion of an action or the receipt of information from another party to proceed with their legal tasks or responsibilities.

properties.name: R8I1TsGJ5eFwM8qAzethrIm
properties.label: sali:interpreted
properties.definition: In a legal context, "interpreted" refers to the process by which legal professionals, especially judges and lawyers, examine and elucidate the meaning or intention of legal texts, such as statutes, contracts, or judicial decisions. This activity involves applying legal principles and precedents to clarify ambiguities, reconcile conflicts, or discern the underlying purpose of the text.

properties.name: R8LI2NysCz4Juz9QDWeZJoE
properties.label: sali:hasEffectiveDate
properties.definition: "Has Effective Date" refers to a specified date when a legal document, contract, or legislative act becomes operative and enforceable. This date marks the beginning of legal obligations, rights, or effects as stipulated in the document or law.

properties.name: R8RerFcbBaYGo4DFhYqoXBC
properties.label: sali:superseded
properties.definition: "Superseded" refers to the act of replacing or nullifying a previous legal rule, decision, or practice with a new one that holds precedence. For example, when a statute supersedes a judicial opinion, it means the new law takes precedence over and effectively replaces the principles or rulings established in that opinion.

properties.name: R8S1bzMuLtlMmrancwPOUSo
properties.label: sali:found
properties.definition: In a legal context, "found" refers to the determination or conclusion reached by a decisionmaker (e.g., judge or jury) regarding the existence of facts, the truth of assertions, the credibility of witnesses, or the guilt of a defendant. This term encapsulates the act of making a judgment or decision based on the evaluation of evidence and testimony.

properties.name: R8ScqoB2b4ln92ntLeQCE3Y
properties.label: sali:hasObligation
properties.definition: In legal terms, "has obligation" refers to the duty or responsibility imposed on an individual, entity, or party by law, contract, or agreement. This obligation can be towards another party, as in contractual commitments, or towards the state or society, such as adhering to criminal laws. Fulfillment of these obligations is legally enforceable, and failure to meet them can result in legal consequences. This concept indicates the direction in which the obligation flows.

properties.name: R8oVqWGVPjAgl133D0pNL7g
properties.label: sali:examined
properties.definition: In legal terms, "examined" refers to the thorough and systematic investigation or inspection of evidence, documents, or facts relevant to a legal case or issue. This process is crucial for lawyers, judges, and legal staff in assessing the validity, relevance, and implications of the materials at hand, often to establish the foundation for arguments or judgments.

properties.name: R8xpRHcxf8y8ru3RmqO4KMx
properties.label: sali:audited
properties.definition: In the legal and regulatory context, "audited" refers to the systematic examination and evaluation of financial records, operational processes, or compliance practices by an independent party. This process is designed to verify accuracy, adherence to standards or regulations, and to assess the effectiveness of internal controls or procedures.

properties.name: R9HWPnaugvaUXld2x3xH2hX
properties.label: sali:greaterThanOrEqualTo
properties.definition: An operator that returns items where the field's value is greater than or equal to the specified value.

properties.name: R9KSG54ZD5NJGhEKjpDjZvO
properties.label: sali:represented
properties.definition: "Represented" in a legal context refers to the act of acting on behalf of another person or entity in legal matters. This involves a representative, such as a lawyer, advocating, making decisions, or taking actions under the authority and in the interest of the represented party.

properties.name: R9OCJDSLZnUbVwWxu2ddA5J
properties.label: sali:affirmed
properties.definition: In the context of appellate law, "affirmed" refers to the decision of an appellate court to uphold the ruling or decision of a lower court. This signifies that, upon review, the appellate court has found no significant legal error in the lower court's handling of the case and agrees with the conclusion reached.

properties.name: R9OgtSm35ykpUSi7mgiCW
properties.label: sali:authenticated
properties.definition: "Authenticated" in a legal setting refers to the process of verifying the genuineness and validity of a document or signature, typically by an authorized person or entity. This verification establishes the document's legitimacy, ensuring it has not been altered and is what it purports to be, often a prerequisite for legal recognition and enforceability.

properties.name: R9RiRk1LnffWe0xUY0IHsmL
properties.label: sali:isGovernedBy
properties.definition: In the legal framework, "governed by" refers to the regulation, control, or direction of legal matters, processes, or entities by specific laws, rules, or principles. This term indicates that a particular area of law or legal procedure is subject to and must comply with established guidelines, standards, or constitutional provisions.

properties.name: R9W9JEOuk0H3iu0X5kmhYoi
properties.label: sali:overruled
properties.definition: In legal practice, "overruled" refers to the action of a higher court setting aside or nullifying the decision of a lower court or an earlier court. Or it could apply to a judge overruling an evidentiary objection. This denotes a rejection of the previous decision or objection based on legal grounds, signaling a different interpretation or application of the law.

properties.name: R9ZUmvtgrZzXkfqfKcFobwZ
properties.label: sali:isSecuredBy
properties.definition: In financial and legal contexts, "is secured by" refers to a debt or obligation that is backed by collateral or a specific asset. This means that if the debtor fails to meet their obligations, the creditor has the right to seize the collateral to recover the owed amount. The presence of collateral provides security for the lender and can affect the terms and conditions of the debt.

properties.name: R9aTcuLVmH38aqd3WcPuzCT
properties.label: sali:supported
properties.definition: In the context of an argument, "supported" refers to the backing or justification provided for a particular claim or assertion using evidence, logical reasoning, or relevant facts. A well-supported argument is strengthened by its corroborating information, making it more persuasive and credible to its audience.

properties.name: R9dR7mByjtP9Tx4NUZI84iO
properties.label: sali:disapproved
properties.definition: In legal contexts, "disapproved" refers to the expression of judicial disagreement or disfavor towards a decision or reasoning of another court, without necessarily overturning or reversing it. This indicates a divergence in legal opinion or interpretation, often noted by higher courts in their rulings or dicta, which can influence future case law without directly changing the immediate case outcome.

properties.name: R9e8PXI2IEusTTC9xKXN7hA
properties.label: sali:isAdverseTo
properties.definition: In legal terminology, "is adverse to" describes a relationship characterized by opposition, conflict, or differing interests between parties in a legal context. This typically applies to situations where one party's interests, claims, or actions are directly opposed to those of another party, as in litigation, contractual disputes, or criminal proceedings.

properties.name: R9g1ytIVLnV6isR8zHgHrdH
properties.label: sali:wasFiledIn
properties.definition: "Was Filed In" in legal terms refers to the act of submitting a legal document, application, or motion to a specific court, tribunal, or administrative body. This term denotes the location or entity where the document was officially lodged and is used to specify the jurisdiction or authority handling the matter.

properties.name: R9iq8MqpS503pOZr7pZiOUb
properties.label: sali:appendedTo
properties.definition: "Appended to" in legal documentation refers to the act of adding supplementary material, such as exhibits, amendments, or additional documents, to an existing legal document or record. This process is crucial for incorporating new or relevant information that supports, clarifies, or modifies the original content, ensuring the document's completeness and accuracy.

properties.name: R9u6A5ODwWnB3Ll5fenny6E
properties.label: sali:isUsedFor
properties.definition: Relationship declaring how one item (e.g., `Tool` like `Westlaw` or `vLex`) might be used for another item (e.g., `Legal Research`).

properties.name: R9yYkx0gjxfCeiErY01Coeq
properties.label: sali:lessThanOrEqualTo
properties.definition: An operator that returns items where the field's value is less than or equal to the specified value.

properties.name: RB0hju1karAVIAsSqkf1Pza
properties.label: sali:obtained
properties.definition: To obtain an artifact (e.g., document, evidence) or a legal result (e.g., judgment, sanctions). In legal and administrative contexts, "obtained" refers to the successful acquisition or securing of a legal status, permission, or qualification by an individual or entity. This term indicates that the individual or entity has met the necessary criteria or completed the required procedures to gain a particular right, privilege, or certification, such as asylum, a professional license, or licensure to practice law.

properties.name: RB3G15ZJPz6X2117zd9FBzc
properties.label: sali:canceled
properties.definition: Canceled refers to the termination or annulment of a legal or administrative action, such as a registration or a hearing. This can occur due to various reasons, including withdrawal by the applicant, failure to meet legal requirements, or administrative decisions.

properties.name: RB7sOdTG7h6T898uKuEAXpP
properties.label: sali:canAccept
properties.definition: In legal and business terms, "can accept" refers to the capacity or legal authority of a party to agree to a proposal, offer, or contract. This involves having the requisite legal competence, authority, and in some cases, the necessary legal capacity, to enter into a binding agreement or to consent to certain terms.

properties.name: RB8dNjfQNfdFxTUkao2ImJ5
properties.label: sali:preparedFor
properties.definition: In legal and business contexts, "prepared for" refers to the act of making ready or getting equipped for a specific event, process, or encounter. This includes activities like researching, strategizing, organizing resources, and planning.

properties.name: RB9WPZAmqztZGzX1qXk6gXv
properties.label: sali:respondedTo
properties.definition: "Responded To" in legal contexts refers to the action of replying or reacting to a legal action, request, or communication. This includes formal legal responses such as answering a lawsuit, replying to a legal notice, or reacting to a court's order, and is crucial for the continuation and progression of legal processes.

properties.name: RB9zpRJFhAzcELy6OTNxqNT
properties.label: sali:ruledUpon
properties.definition: "Ruled Upon" in legal contexts refers to the act of making a formal decision or judgment by a judicial authority, such as a judge, on a particular matter or motion presented in court. This involves the application of legal principles and reasoning to reach a conclusion that resolves a legal question or directs the course of legal proceedings.

properties.name: RBA9fhC1klxcqUb2bMFIIre
properties.label: sali:lessThan
properties.definition: An operator that returns items where the field's value is less than the given value.

properties.name: RBBJ16zFnIqfmkVet3IuV6Z
properties.label: sali:hasEndedDate
properties.definition: "Has Ended Date" refers to the specific date on which a legal document, contract, or obligation ceases to be in effect. This marks the conclusion of the legal validity or enforceability of the document or agreement, signifying the end of rights and responsibilities under its terms.

properties.name: RBDO4YSpOqTwGQp3QqhtPmq
properties.label: sali:abrogated
properties.definition: In legal terms, "abrogated" refers to the formal repeal, nullification, or abolition of a law, regulation, legal decision, or agreement. This action signifies the complete removal or invalidation of the legal force of the abrogated item, often due to changes in circumstances, new legislation, or shifts in legal interpretation.

properties.name: RBHS8Lk6WR8ctm4HdZNPGd9
properties.label: sali:completed
properties.definition: In a legal framework, "completed" refers to the finalization or conclusion of a legal task, process, or document. This term indicates that all necessary actions, procedures, or requirements have been fulfilled, bringing an aspect of the work to a close and often rendering it effective or enforceable.

properties.name: RBMCuIWgiYrteeawprjAlsX
properties.label: sali:replaced
properties.definition: "Replaced" in a legal or administrative context refers to the act of substituting one item, individual, agreement, or legal document with another. This process involves the removal or cessation of the original entity or item's role or function, and its subsequent substitution with a new or updated equivalent.

properties.name: RBNqARoAvfKJ3sr0sPHzvZI
properties.label: has figure collection
properties.definition: a collection of figures

properties.name: RBPsxBT931DDyTjxIBVJgE0
properties.label: sali:isMemberOf
properties.definition: In legal and organizational contexts, "is member of" signifies the belonging or inclusion of an individual or entity in a specific group, committee, board, or organization. This denotes that the individual or entity has a role, responsibilities, rights, or a position within the collective body, subject to its rules, objectives, and governance structure.

properties.name: RBW19bsnBOwINS8K601XYsz
properties.label: sali:attended
properties.definition: In a legal context, "attended" refers to the act of being present at a legal event, such as a court hearing, meeting, or negotiation. This presence, whether physical or virtual, signifies participation or observation in legal proceedings or discussions, which is often crucial for understanding, contributing to, or complying with legal processes.

properties.label: sali:operators
properties.definition: Operators are search-related logical tools used in databases to refine and direct search queries. They control the relationship between search terms.

properties.name: RBhFi0XLvhq8d4QdZMZ42x9
properties.label: sali:registered
properties.definition: "Registered" refers to the official recording or enrollment of an item, entity, or individual in a formal registry by an authoritative body. This process provides legal recognition and may confer certain rights, responsibilities, or status, such as intellectual property protection for patents or legal authority to practice for attorneys

properties.name: RBlvKceLVwnUflJvHuHBpSO
properties.label: sali:denied
properties.definition: In legal contexts, "denied" refers to the rejection or refusal of a request, motion, application, or claim by a judicial or administrative authority. This decision indicates that the request does not meet the necessary legal criteria, is unfounded, or is otherwise not suitable for approval or granting under the prevailing legal framework.

properties.name: RBnpEtVTcX8UHPGSPPAzf1w
properties.label: sali:greaterThan
properties.definition: An operator that returns items where the specified field's value is greater than the given value.

properties.name: RBu87FXpegbtFY5SjoXRe29
properties.label: sali:isInitial
properties.definition: "Is Initial" in a legal or administrative context refers to the first or original version of a document or agreement before any amendments, revisions, or updates. This term denotes the baseline from which any changes are measured, often serving as a reference point in legal analysis or when modifications are made.

properties.name: RBvy26hKlSPzCVJMlWTlBQb
properties.label: sali:verified
properties.definition: "Verified" in a legal context refers to the process of confirming the accuracy, authenticity, or truthfulness of information, statements, or documents. This involves examining and validating the content to ensure it aligns with factual data, legal standards, or specified criteria, often essential in legal proceedings and documentation.

properties.name: RBwcSq7zBAAVljlAwwbMjoq
properties.label: sali:appearedBefore
properties.definition: "Appeared before" in legal parlance refers to the formal presentation or representation of a party or their legal counsel in front of a judicial body, such as a court or a judge. This term signifies the physical or legal presence required for proceedings, ranging from hearings to trials, where legal matters are argued, evidence is presented, and rulings are made.

properties.name: RBzcoqc9gDSOGkNUDhDfDV
properties.label: filled by
properties.definition: an Actor that fills the Role.

properties.name: RBzfLJrwPMpX5k3ZuyirpzI
properties.label: sali:hasElement
properties.definition: In legal terminology, "has element" refers to the essential components or criteria that must be established to prove a legal claim or defense. Each element is a necessary part of the legal theory that must be demonstrated for the claim to be legally valid. For instance, a breach of contract claim requires proving elements like the existence of a contract, breach of its terms, and resulting damages.

properties.name: RC3qfiYtXVNQmnmcuYjcVIj
properties.label: sali:and
properties.definition: Default for multiple SALI tags. For example, if a query filters for `A B C`, then implied is the query `A sali:and B sali:and C`.  A logical conjunction operator that combines search terms, returning items that match all of the terms.

properties.name: RCDOABUr8ZTMQ7N7Rydeius
properties.label: sali:signed
properties.definition: "Signed" in a legal context refers to the act of putting one's signature on a legal document, such as a pleading, contract, or order. This signature signifies the individual's approval, authorization, or acknowledgement of the content of the document, and is often a requisite for the document's legal validity and enforceability.

properties.name: RCDx1OyD4xo9Pj6dWOBMStt
properties.label: sali:temporalChanges
properties.definition: "Temporal Changes" in legal contexts refer to the various time-related aspects and milestones that affect the status, applicability, or relevance of legal documents, agreements, or decisions.

properties.name: RCFpktWEZOtDt2qAABUgJ8H
properties.label: sali:asserted
properties.definition: "Asserted" in a legal context refers to the act of confidently stating or declaring a fact, right, or legal position, typically as part of a legal claim or defense. This assertion forms the basis of a party's argument or claim in legal proceedings, setting the stage for the legal debate and burden of proof. Compared with the more-argumentative terms "opposed" or "supported," the term "asserted" is more neutral.

properties.name: RCFxbmwYw4z5dXO2SvKw1nI
properties.label: sali:dismissed
properties.definition: In legal practice, "dismissed" refers to the action taken by a court or judicial panel to terminate a case, claim, or appeal. This decision can be based on procedural grounds, lack of jurisdiction, non-compliance with legal requirements, or other reasons that render the case unsuitable for continuation.

properties.name: RCP3eyKInCMJp5Fv01RmL3u
properties.label: sali:isDefending
properties.definition: Defense of Deposition refers to the strategic and legal actions taken by a party's attorney to protect their client during a deposition. The attorney seeks to guide the deponent in providing accurate but limited information, objecting to inappropriate questions, and ensuring that the deposition serves the best interests of the client.

properties.name: RCR0ohH8RV8nUH2c7aS9ERM
properties.label: sali:similar
properties.definition: Operator that returns items that are similar to the search term, potentially including synonyms, fuzzy matches, and semantically related terms.

properties.name: RCTNn1zYwKrZiAMp1rQkjx2
properties.label: sali:decided
properties.definition: In the legal arena, "decided" refers to the process of reaching a conclusion or verdict in a legal matter or legal document. This term encompasses various outcomes such as acceptance, affirmation, denial, or dismissal, representing the authoritative resolution or determination made by a court or tribunal.

properties.name: RCadgGcfBZxaL64cSvVk2dq
properties.label: sali:vacated
properties.definition: In legal practice, "vacated" refers to the annulment or setting aside of a court decision, order, or judgment by a judicial authority. This term implies that the previous decision is rendered null and void, often due to procedural errors, legal inconsistencies, or new evidence that fundamentally alters the case's dynamics.

properties.name: RCagJhRyGTd2hJN5QTrg7Ru
properties.label: sali:approved
properties.definition: "Approved" in a legal context signifies the formal acceptance or endorsement of a document, action, or decision by an authorized individual or body. This approval usually indicates compliance with legal standards or requirements and often signifies the finalization of a legal process, agreement, or decision.

properties.name: RCcfFsMP7IYtjlfdSBJmKNF
properties.label: sali:stemming
properties.definition: Operator that returns variations of a word based on its stem (e.g., query for the stem "run" would result in "runs", "running", "runner").

properties.name: RCdPQDV9TEe33ydDVVkGQyf
properties.label: sali:testified
properties.definition: "Testified" in a legal context refers to the act of giving evidence or a statement under oath in a court of law or a legal proceeding. This process is vital for presenting factual information and personal accounts to the court, helping in the establishment or disputation of facts critical to the resolution of legal disputes.

properties.name: RCeIFhdEEtecwLgAYEoAxPX
properties.label: sali:advised
properties.definition: In legal contexts, "advised" refers to the provision of professional legal counsel or recommendations to clients, based on the interpretation of the law and its application to specific circumstances. This process is critical in guiding clients through legal complexities, ensuring informed decision-making and compliance with legal norms and obligations.

properties.name: RCfGltyATZDch3La86F79hq
properties.label: sali:granted
properties.definition: In the legal sphere, "granted" refers to the approval or acceptance of a request, motion, or appeal by a judicial authority. This term indicates that the court has agreed to the request, whether it's for procedural actions like a motion in a trial, or substantive issues like granting a writ of certiorari in appellate courts.

properties.name: RCmX2a3aVJOIgpjsiRggnxX
properties.label: sali:presented
properties.definition: In legal contexts, "presented" refers to the act of formally introducing or submitting evidence, arguments, or information in a judicial or legal setting. This encompasses the delivery of material in a structured and often persuasive manner, essential for informing the decision-making process or supporting a legal claim or defense.

properties.name: RCrkDVNXup86PCJ1li7GrFx
properties.label: sali:departed
properties.definition: Departure from a location, by a person or object, which can have litigation, immigration, tax, and other regulatory effects.

properties.name: RCuyvwwZzhCRHWEZZVIlpHF
properties.label: sali:isCurrencyFor
properties.definition: In economic and legal contexts, "is currency for" denotes that a specific form of money is officially recognized and used as the medium of exchange within a particular country or region. For example, the U.S. Dollar is the standard unit for pricing and transactions in the United States, and that currency holds legal backing from its government.

properties.name: RCx3rNyJdykIdu45Cr4ajaK
properties.label: sali:appealsTo
properties.definition: "Appeals to" in a legal setting refers to the process of challenging and seeking review of a lower court's decision by a higher court. This action is initiated by the party dissatisfied with the trial court's judgment, aiming for a reassessment of the legal and factual determinations made, based on the assertion of errors in the application of law or procedural missteps. It also relates to where a case heard by a trial court "appeals to" the appellate court (e.g., SDNY appeals to Second Circuit).

properties.name: RDC4DqaMFIcuowN8mPKfzE5
properties.label: sali:near
properties.definition: Specifies a proximity search operator, used to find items that are close to each other (within a certain distance) in a text

properties.name: RDGdDmBhMZICUDoXt6HEEbr
properties.label: sali:hastype
properties.definition: RIEHL NOTE: This was originally conceived as a `New York Courts sali:hasType Dispute Forum` but that will likely be deprecated in favor of having Courts be Individuals (not Classes).

properties.name: RDHwdM2A0beLXWa3uCOuj18
properties.label: sali:applied
properties.definition: In a legal setting, "applied" refers to the act of implementing or utilizing legal principles, caselaw, statutes, or rules in the decision-making process. This involves interpreting the relevant law and integrating it into the resolution of a case, whether by a judge, arbitrator, or jury.

properties.name: RDKLC9VaaCYFPmyFrTjNTd5
properties.label: sali:contains
properties.definition: Indicates an operator that searches for items containing a specific substring or sequence.

properties.name: RDNoruauHZ4Tn1JNgobdmol
properties.label: sali:concerning
properties.definition: (Hearing) sali:concerning (Motion) sali:concerning (Summary Judgment)

properties.name: RDSBgWxWYHvX1IXdqrnXOT
properties.label: DEPRECATED FAVORING AFFIRMED sali:upheld
properties.definition: In legal terms, "upheld" refers to the decision of a court, especially an appellate court, to confirm and maintain the ruling or decision of a lower court. This indicates that, upon review, the appellate court found the original decision to be correct and in accordance with the law, warranting no change or reversal.

properties.name: RDVFemXaqT513UrGRVhWDSH
properties.label: sali:hasNext
properties.definition: In the context of legal ontologies and processes, "has next" refers to the sequential relationship where a specific legal event or task is followed by another predetermined event or task. This concept denotes the procedural order or chronology within legal proceedings. For example, "jury selection has next trial" implies that the jury selection phase in a trial precedes the actual commencement of the trial proceedings.

properties.name: RDc1B2GDj6ckfXBkRRSJXfH
properties.label: TR:SALI
properties.definition: Mapping between Thomson Reuters concepts (i.e., labels, identifiers) and SALI concepts.

properties.name: RDexpiWmmK9xFb7iMaBJpcD
properties.label: sali:reverted
properties.definition: In legal contexts, "reverted" refers to the act of returning to a previous state, condition, or set of circumstances, often as a result of a judicial decision or the operation of law. This term is typically used when rights, property, or legal status are restored to their former condition, either due to contractual stipulations, legal provisions, or court orders.

properties.name: RDg3svGlPQWSeM8eDKzJTSf
properties.label: sali:hasExpense
properties.definition: In legal and professional contexts, "has expense" refers to the incurrence of costs or financial outlays associated with performing certain actions or fulfilling duties. This includes expenditures such as travel costs for depositions, purchasing materials for expert analysis, or other necessary expenses incurred in the course of legal representation or consultation.

properties.name: RDkNxLSVfcWlNUKatMJwnMt
properties.label: sali:filed
properties.definition: In legal procedures, "filed" refers to the formal submission of documents, such as lawsuits, motions, or applications, to a court, agency, or other official body. This act initiates or progresses legal proceedings and is a critical step in ensuring that legal matters are officially recorded, recognized, and acted upon according to relevant laws and regulations.

properties.name: RDl0w1bStTabxjJhVmoyAO8
properties.label: sali:isSubsequent
properties.definition: "Is Subsequent" in legal and procedural contexts refers to something that follows or comes after something else, particularly in a sequence of events, documents, or legal actions. This term is used to describe a version, action, or decision that occurs or is produced after a preceding one, indicating its place in a chronological or logical order.

properties.name: RDxHHUOM1v4NOmByelkNw11
properties.label: sali:hasSignedDate
properties.definition: "Has Signed Date" refers to the specific date on which a contract, agreement, judicial opinion, or other legal document was signed. This date is often marks the commencement of rights, responsibilities, and terms outlined in the document.

properties.name: RDyfwuKf33mCj2gfpqW702n
properties.label: sali:or
properties.definition: A logical operator that combines search terms to retrieve items that match any of the terms.

properties.name: RH73qlQGajAwUFNMEkH9T2
properties.label: sali:binaryOperators
properties.definition: A category of operators that use two operands, such as the comparison of numerical values (e.g., GreaterThan, LessThan, EqualTo, NotEqualTo).

properties.name: RHfRMWirAE49F9Widnyd7V
properties.label: sali:directExamined
properties.definition: In the legal realm, "direct examined" refers to the initial questioning of a witness by the party that called them to testify in a trial or hearing. This process is fundamental for establishing the facts of a case as presented by the witness, and it focuses on eliciting favorable, relevant testimony in a narrative form, typically without leading questions.

properties.name: RI8E8tMRzJgno8mZ763EPv
properties.label: sali:notEqual
properties.definition: An operator that returns items where the field's value does not match the given value.

properties.name: RMQvvbEUbz97RKKfKnpOTl
properties.label: sali:requested
properties.definition: "Requested" in legal terms refers to the act of formally asking for something within a legal context, such as information, action, or a particular legal remedy. This typically involves a formal application or petition to a court, agency, or another party, outlining the specifics of what is being sought and the grounds for the request.

properties.name: RN3mWlXZUAt07dYsu6tls2
properties.label: sali:seeksToAchieve
properties.definition: "Seeks to Achieve" refers to the act of pursuing a specific legal outcome or objective. This involves drafting, arguing, and advocating for legal legal goals (e.g., preliminary injunction, securing indemnification).

properties.name: RQibzWMnQMD73BO19CWUPt
properties.label: sali:sent
properties.definition: "Sent" in a legal context refers to the act of dispatching or transmitting a communication or document from one party to another.

properties.name: RRmQYyvtQ35FVexIVWZnyn
properties.label: sali:crossExamined
properties.definition: "Cross examined" in legal contexts denotes the rigorous questioning of a witness by the opposing party, often following their direct examination by the party who called them. This process is a critical aspect of the adversarial system, aimed at challenging the credibility, reliability, and consistency of the witness's testimony, often through pointed, leading questions.

properties.name: RSUYYgxaSZBNickjaRAqzJ
properties.label: sali:codified
properties.definition: In the legislative and legal context, "codified" refers to the process by which laws, rules, or regulations are systematically collected, arranged, and published in a formal legal code. This act of codification transforms various statutes, ordinances, and legal principles into an organized and accessible format, often to provide clarity, consistency, and ease of reference.

properties.name: RSvfP5xuO21mAI4NS6EbLP
properties.label: sali:distinguished
properties.definition: In legal analysis, "distinguished" refers to the process of demonstrating how a current case or situation differs from a previous case, legal proposition, or fact pattern. This is often done by judges or arbitrators to justify a different legal outcome or application of law, despite apparent similarities to earlier precedents or scenarios.

properties.name: RTVHIHUY48KidG92GXtTlH
properties.label: sali:hasSubsidiary
properties.definition: In corporate law and business, "has subsidiary" refers to the relationship where a parent company owns and controls a separate and distinct company, known as a subsidiary. This denotes that the subsidiary operates as an independent entity but is under the significant influence or control of the parent corporation, both in management and often in financial matters.

properties.name: RUBi4AYhUtpu5FhXaia36Q
properties.label: sali:notarized
properties.definition: In legal terms, "notarized" refers to the process where a document is officially certified by a notary public, a licensed official who verifies the identity of the signatories and their understanding and willingness to sign the document. This process lends authenticity and legal weight to the document, often required for legal formalities such as property deeds, wills, and contracts.

properties.name: RUmf4RiyCyjE8hwApkfp6o
properties.label: sali:researched
properties.definition: "Researched" in a legal context refers to the systematic investigation or study of legal documents, case law, statutes, and other legal sources to gather information, understand legal precedents, and develop legal arguments. This process is fundamental for lawyers, legal scholars, and other professionals to build a thorough understanding of legal issues, cases, and the legal framework.

properties.name: RVcCszu01sLSiXW2CvBBE7
properties.label: sali:reviewed
properties.definition: "Reviewed" in a legal setting refers to the examination and evaluation of legal documents, motions, or evidence. This process, often undertaken by judges, lawyers, or legal officials, involves a thorough analysis to understand the content, assess its relevance and validity, and determine its impact on a legal matter or decision.

properties.name: RWd966Up5VVRxKPkv1PPBZ
properties.label: sali:certified
properties.definition: In a legal context, "certified" refers to the formal declaration or confirmation by a competent authority that a document, process, or individual meets established standards or criteria. This certification process is crucial for establishing the authenticity, accuracy, or qualification of the subject matter, often required for legal compliance, recognition, or enforcement.

properties.name: RXvlgtHqXTWS2UvbLmm6JD
properties.label: sali:hasBenefit
properties.definition: Who has the benefit of an item? EXAMPLE: Whom does Contractual Directionality benefit? Example:  Party A indemnifying Party B benefits Party B. Example: Party A receiving Party B's goods benefits Party A.

properties.name: RZSnKehA643O8824iC320g
properties.label: sali:workedFor
properties.definition: "Worked For" refers to the employment or professional relationship where an individual, such as a lawyer or paralegal, is engaged in duties or services for an entity like a court, a judge, or a law firm. This term encompasses the scope of professional activities undertaken by the individual under the employment or direction of the specified legal entity or employer.

properties.name: RdAgrsvdn5d59nUUq1iU9D
properties.label: sali:took
properties.definition: "Took" in various legal contexts encompasses the action of acquiring, obtaining, or accepting something. That can include taking property, solemnly accepting something (e.g., oath), or taking evidence (e.g., testimony).

properties.name: RdpSPh3bFHYrQ3vYPDwJYB
properties.label: sali:cited
properties.definition: In legal contexts, "cited" refers to the act of referencing or quoting authoritative sources such as caselaw, statutes, documents, or prior testimony to support arguments, claims, or positions. This practice is common in legal reasoning and advocacy, providing evidential or jurisprudential backing to the points being made.

properties.name: RebIkaU3BW0LoMNlSf8DQ3
properties.label: DEPRECATED FAVORING REMANDED sali:remitted
properties.definition: In legal terminology, "remit" refers to the act of a higher court sending a case back to a lower court for further action, reconsideration, or a new trial. This typically occurs after an appellate review, where the appellate court has identified specific issues that require additional examination or resolution by the lower court.

properties.name: RfM1fbV2yfBPHRkAlT1o3o
properties.label: sali:destroyed
properties.definition: To destroy an artifact. Example: Party destroyed evidence. Example: Provider destroyed a Buyer's (e.g., a client's) closed and dormant file. Example: Party destroyed data according to its Document Retention Policy.

properties.name: Ri6OrmVAB1fhqFK0qdbch
properties.label: sali:discontinued
properties.definition: In the legal realm, "discontinued" refers to the cessation or termination of a legal action, process, or proceeding before its natural conclusion. This typically occurs when the party initiating the action decides to halt proceedings, which can be due to various reasons such as a settlement, a change in circumstances, or a reassessment of the likelihood of success.

properties.name: RlWWALyEkmi7ifaz2MpmoR
properties.label: sali:remanded
properties.definition: "Remanded" in legal practice refers to the decision of a higher court to send a case back to a lower court for additional action, further proceedings, or a new decision. This often occurs when an appellate court finds that the lower court made a procedural error, or when additional fact-finding or legal analysis is necessary.

properties.name: Rrs38f6iVq0CeArcJaGhwR
properties.label: sali:arrived
properties.definition: Arrival at a location, by a person or object, which can have litigation, immigration, tax, and other regulatory effects.

properties.name: Rtcn744oelK5y1pAR0epCQ
properties.label: sali:rejected
properties.definition: In legal proceedings, "rejected" refers to the decision of an authority (judicial, arbitral, administrative) to not accept an argument, testimony, evidence, document, or claim presented. This implies that the presented material is deemed unpersuasive, insufficient, irrelevant, or inadmissible under legal standards or specific case requirements.

properties.name: RwdlnXbLIUXj4VeNyet8FP
properties.label: has agent collection
properties.definition: a collection of Agents

properties.name: RznfymBGs7WesrwWNzQLov
properties.label: sali:participatedIn
properties.definition: "Participated in" within a legal framework refers to active involvement in a legal proceeding or activity, such as a hearing, deposition, or negotiation. This term encompasses not just physical presence but also engagement in the process, contributing through actions like presenting arguments, giving testimony, or collaborating in discussions.

types.label: Other Personal and Household Goods Repair and Maintenance
types.definition: See industry description for 811490.

types.label: Other Converted Paper Product Manufacturing
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in (1) converting paper and paperboard into products (except containers, bags, coated and treated paper and paperboard, and stationery products) or (2) converting pulp into pulp products, such as disposable diapers, or molded pulp egg cartons, food trays, and dishes.  Processes used include laminating or lining purchased paper or paperboard.

types.label: Confectionery Merchant Wholesalers
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in the merchant wholesale distribution of confectioneries; salted or roasted nuts; popcorn; potato, corn, and similar chips; and/or fountain fruits and syrups.

types.label: Other Specialized Design Services
types.definition: See industry description for 541490.

types.label: Deep Sea, Coastal, and Great Lakes Water Transportation
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing deep sea, coastal, Great Lakes, and St. Lawrence Seaway water transportation.  Marine transportation establishments using the facilities of the St. Lawrence Seaway Authority Commission are considered to be using the Great Lakes Water Transportation System.

types.label: Turkey Production
types.definition: See industry description for 112330.

types.label: Other Gambling Industries
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in operating gambling facilities (except casinos or casino hotels) or providing gambling services.

types.label: Other Miscellaneous Nondurable Goods Merchant Wholesalers
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in the merchant wholesale distribution of nondurable goods (except printing and writing paper; stationery and office supplies; industrial and personal service paper; drugs and druggists' sundries; apparel, piece goods, and notions; grocery and related products; farm product raw materials; chemical and allied products; petroleum and petroleum products; beer, wine, and distilled alcoholic beverages; farm supplies; books, periodicals, and newspapers; flowers, nursery stock, and florists' supplies; tobacco and tobacco products; and paint, varnishes, wallpaper, and supplies).

types.label: Chocolate and Confectionery Manufacturing from Cacao Beans
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in shelling, roasting, and grinding cacao beans and making chocolate cacao products and chocolate confectioneries.

types.label: Mechanical Power Transmission Equipment Manufacturing
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing mechanical power transmission equipment (except motor vehicle and aircraft), such as plain bearings, clutches (except motor vehicle and electromagnetic industrial control), couplings, joints, and drive chains.

types.label: Commercial and Service Industry Machinery Manufacturing
types.definition: See industry description for 333310.

types.label: Frozen Specialty Food Manufacturing
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing frozen specialty foods (except seafood), such as frozen dinners, entrees, and side dishes; frozen pizza; frozen whipped topping; and frozen waffles, pancakes, and French toast.

types.label: Ophthalmic Goods Manufacturing
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing ophthalmic goods. Examples of products made by these establishments are prescription eyeglasses (except grinding lenses in a retail setting), contact lenses, sunglasses, eyeglass frames, reading glasses made to standard powers, and protective eyewear.

types.label: All Other Grain Farming
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in growing grains and/or producing grain(s) seeds (except wheat, corn, rice, and oilseed(s) and grain(s) combinations).

types.label: Fish and Seafood Merchant Wholesalers
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in the merchant wholesale distribution of fish and seafood (except canned or packaged frozen).

types.label: Commercial Banking Industry
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in accepting demand and other deposits and making commercial, industrial, and consumer loans. Commercial banks and branches of foreign banks are included in this industry.

types.label: Other Miscellaneous Durable Goods Merchant Wholesalers
types.definition: See industry description for 423990.

types.label: Bread and Bakery Product Manufacturing
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing fresh and frozen bread and other bakery products.

types.label: Other Metal Valve and Pipe Fitting Manufacturing
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing metal valves (except industrial valves, fluid power valves, fluid power hose fittings, and plumbing fixture fittings and trim).

types.label: All Other Transportation Equipment Manufacturing
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing transportation equipment (except motor vehicles, motor vehicle parts, boats, ships, railroad rolling stock, aerospace products, motorcycles, bicycles, armored vehicles, and tanks).

types.label: Convenience Retailers and Vending Machine Operators
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in retailing a limited line of groceries that generally includes milk, bread, soda, and snacks.  Included in this industry are convenience retailers, such as convenience stores or food marts (except those operating fuel pumps), and vending machine operators.

types.label: Commercial Bakeries
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing fresh and frozen bread and bread-type rolls and other fresh bakery (except cookies and crackers) products.

types.label: Polystyrene Foam Product Manufacturing
types.definition: See industry description for 326140.

types.label: Copper Rolling, Drawing, Extruding, and Alloying
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in one or more of the following: (1) recovering copper or copper alloys from scraps; (2) alloying purchased copper; (3) rolling, drawing, or extruding shapes (e.g., bar, plate, sheet, strip, tube, wire) from purchased copper; and (4) recovering copper or copper alloys from scrap and rolling, drawing, or extruding shapes (e.g., bar, plate, sheet, strip, tube, wire).

types.label: Gypsum Product Manufacturing
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing gypsum products, such as wallboard, plaster, plasterboard, molding, ornamental moldings, statuary, and architectural plaster work. Gypsum product manufacturing establishments may mine, quarry, or purchase gypsum.

types.label: Other Grocery and Related Products Merchant Wholesalers
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in the merchant wholesale distribution of groceries and related products (except a general line of groceries; packaged frozen food; dairy products (except dried and canned); poultry products (except canned); confectioneries; fish and seafood (except canned); meat products (except canned); and fresh fruits and vegetables). Included in this industry are establishments primarily engaged in the bottling and merchant wholesale distribution of spring and mineral waters processed by others.

types.label: Fruit and Tree Nut Farming
types.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in growing fruit and/or tree nut crops. The crops included in this industry group are generally not grown from seeds and have a perennial life cycle.

types.label: Other Activities Related to Credit Intermediation Industry
types.definition: See industry description for 522390.

types.label: American Indian and Alaska Native Tribal Governments
types.definition: See industry description for 921150.

types.label: Restaurants and Other Eating Places
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in one of the following: (1) providing food services to patrons who order and are served while seated (i.e., waiter/waitress service) and pay after eating; (2) providing food services to patrons who generally order or select items (e.g., at a counter, in a buffet line) and pay before eating; or (3) preparing and/or serving a specialty snack (e.g., ice cream, frozen yogurt, cookies) and/or nonalcoholic beverages (e.g., coffee, juices, sodas) for consumption on or near the premises.

types.label: Advertising Agencies
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in creating advertising campaigns and placing such advertising in print and digital periodicals, newspapers, radio and television, or other media. These establishments are organized to provide a full range of services (i.e., through in-house capabilities or subcontracting), including advice, creative services, account management, production of advertising content, media planning, and buying (i.e., placing advertising).

types.label: Laminated Plastics Plate, Sheet (except Packaging), and Shape Manufacturing
types.definition: See industry description for 326130.

types.label: Flour Milling
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in (1) milling flour or meal from grains (except rice) or vegetables and/or (2) milling flour and preparing flour mixes or doughs.

types.label: Metal Can Manufacturing
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing metal cans, lids, and ends.

types.label: Exam Preparation and Tutoring
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in offering preparation for standardized examinations and/or academic tutoring services.

types.label: Fabric Coating Mills
types.definition: See industry description for 313320.

types.label: Performing Arts Companies
types.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in producing live presentations involving the performances of actors and actresses, singers, dancers, musical groups and artists, and other performing artists.

types.label: Radio Broadcasting Stations
types.definition: See industry description for 516110.

types.label: Adhesive Manufacturing
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing adhesives, glues, and caulking compounds.

types.label: All Other Pipeline Transportation
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in the pipeline transportation of products (except crude oil, natural gas, and refined petroleum products).

types.label: Miscellaneous Manufacturing Industry
types.definition:
Industries in the Miscellaneous Manufacturing subsector make a wide range of products that cannot readily be classified in specific NAICS subsectors in manufacturing.  Processes used by these establishments vary significantly, both among and within industries.  For example, a variety of manufacturing processes are used in manufacturing sporting and athletic goods that include products such as tennis rackets and golf balls.  The processes for these products differ from each other, and the processes differ significantly from the fabrication processes used in making dolls or toys, the melting and shaping of precious metals to make jewelry, and the bending, forming, and assembly used in making medical products.

The industries in this subsector are defined by what is made rather than how it is made.  Although individual establishments might be appropriately classified elsewhere in the NAICS structure, for historical continuity, these product-based industries were maintained.  In most cases, no one process or material predominates for an industry.

Establishments in this subsector manufacture products as diverse as medical equipment and supplies, jewelry, sporting goods, toys, and office supplies.

types.label: Beer, Wine, and Liquor Retailers
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in retailing packaged alcoholic beverages, such as ale, beer, wine, and liquor.

types.label: Household Appliances, Electric Housewares, and Consumer Electronics Merchant Wholesalers
types.definition: See industry description for 423620.

types.label: Engine, Turbine, and Power Transmission Equipment Manufacturing
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing turbines, power transmission equipment, and internal combustion engines (except automotive gasoline and aircraft).

types.label: Scenic and Sightseeing Transportation, Other
types.definition: See industry description for 487990.

types.label: Administration of Human Resource Programs (except Education, Public Health, and Veterans' Affairs Programs)
types.definition: This industry comprises government establishments primarily engaged in the planning, administration, and coordination of programs for public assistance, social work, and welfare activities. The administration of Social Security, disability insurance, Medicare, unemployment insurance, and workers' compensation programs are included in this industry.

types.label: Machinery, Equipment, and Supplies Merchant Wholesalers
types.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in the merchant wholesale distribution of construction, mining, farm, garden, industrial, service establishment, and transportation machinery, equipment, and supplies.

types.label: Sawmills and Wood Preservation
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in one or more of the following: (1) sawing dimension lumber, boards, beams, timber, poles, ties, shingles, shakes, siding, and wood chips from logs or bolts; (2) sawing round wood poles, pilings, and posts and treating them with preservatives; and (3) treating wood sawed, planed, or shaped in other establishments with creosote or other preservatives to prevent decay and to protect against fire and insects.  Sawmills may plane the rough lumber that they make with a planing machine to achieve smoothness and uniformity of size.

types.label: Photographic Film, Paper, Plate, Chemical, and Copy Toner Manufacturing
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing sensitized film, sensitized paper, sensitized cloth, sensitized plates, toners (i.e., for photocopiers, laser printers, and similar electrostatic printing devices), toner cartridges, and photographic chemicals.

types.label: Fish and Seafood Merchant Wholesalers
types.definition: See industry description for 424460.

types.label: Pipeline Transportation of Crude Oil
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in the pipeline transportation of crude oil.

types.label: Charter Bus Industry
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing buses for charter. These establishments provide bus services to meet customers' road transportation needs and generally do not operate over fixed routes and on regular schedules.

types.label: Scheduled Passenger Air Transportation
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing air transportation of passengers or passengers and freight over regular routes and on regular schedules. Establishments in this industry operate flights even if partially loaded. Scheduled air passenger carriers including commuter and helicopter carriers (except scenic and sightseeing) are included in this industry.

types.label: Tour Operators
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in arranging and assembling tours. The tours are sold through travel agencies or tour operators. Travel or wholesale tour operators are included in this industry.

types.label: Automotive Body, Paint, Interior, and Glass Repair
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing one or more of the following: (1) repairing or customizing automotive vehicle and trailer bodies and interiors; (2) painting automotive vehicle and trailer bodies; (3) replacing, repairing, and/or tinting automotive vehicle glass; and (4) customizing automobile, truck, and van interiors for the physically disabled or other customers with special requirements.

types.label: Research and Development in Nanotechnology
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in conducting nanotechnology research and experimental development. Nanotechnology research and experimental development involves the study of matter at the nanoscale (i.e., a scale of about 1 to 100 nanometers). This research and development in nanotechnology may result in development of new nanotechnology processes or in prototypes of new or altered materials and/or products that may be reproduced, utilized, or implemented by various industries.

types.label: Other Warehousing and Storage
types.definition: See industry description for 493190.

types.label: All Other Rubber Product Manufacturing
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing rubber products (except tires; hoses and belting; and molded, extruded, and lathe-cut rubber goods for mechanical applications (except rubber tubing)) from natural and synthetic rubber. Establishments manufacturing rubber tubing made from natural and synthetic rubber, regardless of process used, are included in this industry.

types.label: General Rental Centers
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in renting a range of consumer, commercial, and industrial equipment. Establishments in this industry typically operate from conveniently located facilities where they maintain inventories of goods and equipment that they rent for short periods of time. The type of equipment that establishments in this industry provide often includes, but is not limited to: audio visual equipment, contractors' and builders' tools and equipment, home repair tools, lawn and garden equipment, moving equipment and supplies, and party and banquet equipment and supplies.

types.label: Outdoor Power Equipment Retailers
types.definition: See industry description for 444230.

types.label: Offices of Mental Health Practitioners (except Physicians)
types.definition: See industry description for 621330.

types.label: Other Support Activities for Road Transportation
types.definition: See industry description for 488490.

types.label: Nonwoven Fabric Mills
types.definition: See industry description for 313230.

types.label: Mineral Wool Manufacturing
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing mineral wool and mineral wool (i.e., fiberglass) insulation products made of such siliceous materials as rock, slag, and glass or combinations thereof.

types.label: Periodical Publishers
types.definition: See industry description for 513120.

types.label: Tire Manufacturing
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing tires and inner tubes from natural and synthetic rubber and retreading or rebuilding tires.

types.label: Airport Operations
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in (1) operating international, national, or civil airports or public flying fields or (2) supporting airport operations (except special food services contractors), such as rental of hangar space, air traffic control (except military) services, baggage handling services, and cargo handling services.

types.label: All Other Miscellaneous Ambulatory Health Care Services
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing ambulatory health care services (except offices of physicians, dentists, and other health practitioners; outpatient care centers; medical and diagnostic laboratories; home health care providers; ambulances; and blood and organ banks).

types.label: Shoe Retailers
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in retailing all types of new footwear (except hosiery and specialty sports footwear, such as golf shoes, bowling shoes, and cleated shoes). Establishments primarily engaged in retailing new tennis shoes or sneakers are included in this industry.

types.label: Timber Tract Operations
types.definition: See industry description for 113110.

types.label: Cut Stone and Stone Product Manufacturing
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in cutting, shaping, and finishing granite, marble, limestone, slate, and other stone for building and miscellaneous uses. Stone product manufacturing establishments may mine, quarry, or purchase stone.

types.label: Regulation, Licensing, and Inspection of Miscellaneous Commercial Sectors
types.definition: This industry comprises government establishments primarily engaged in the regulation, licensing, and inspection of commercial sectors, such as retail trade, professional occupations, manufacturing, mining, construction, and services. Included in this industry are government establishments maintaining physical standards, regulating hazardous conditions not elsewhere classified, and enforcing alcoholic beverage control regulations.

types.label: Computer Terminal and Other Computer Peripheral Equipment Manufacturing
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing computer terminals and other computer peripheral equipment (except storage devices).

types.label: Offices of Physicians
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments of health practitioners having the degree of M.D. (Doctor of Medicine) or D.O. (Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine) primarily engaged in the independent practice of general or specialized medicine (e.g., anesthesiology, oncology, ophthalmology, psychiatry) or surgery.  These practitioners operate private or group practices in their own offices (e.g., centers, clinics) or in the facilities of others, such as hospitals or HMO medical centers.

types.label: Landscape Architectural Services
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in planning and designing the development of land areas for projects, such as parks and other recreational areas; airports; highways; hospitals; schools; land subdivisions; and commercial, industrial, and residential areas, by applying knowledge of land characteristics, location of buildings and structures, use of land areas, and design of landscape projects.

types.label: Specialized Freight Trucking
types.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing local or long-distance specialized freight trucking. The establishments of this industry are primarily engaged in the transportation of freight which, because of size, weight, shape, or other inherent characteristics, requires specialized equipment, such as flatbeds, tankers, or refrigerated trailers. This industry includes the transportation of used household, institutional, and commercial furniture and equipment.

types.label: Biological Product (except Diagnostic) Manufacturing
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing vaccines, toxoids, blood fractions, and culture media of plant or animal origin (except diagnostic).

types.label: Roasted Nuts and Peanut Butter Manufacturing
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in one or more of the following: (1) salting, roasting, drying, cooking, or canning nuts; (2) processing grains or seeds into snacks; and (3) manufacturing peanut butter and other nut butters.

types.label: Other Poultry Production
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in raising poultry (except chickens for meat or egg production and turkeys).

types.label: Capacitor, Resistor, Coil, Transformer, and Other Inductor Manufacturing
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in one or more of the following: (1) manufacturing electronic fixed and variable capacitors and condensers; (2) manufacturing electronic resistors, such as fixed and variable resistors, resistor networks, thermistors, and varistors; and (3) manufacturing electronic inductors, such as coils and transformers.

types.label: Theater Companies and Dinner Theaters
types.definition: This industry comprises (1) companies, groups, or theaters primarily engaged in producing the following live theatrical presentations: musicals; operas; plays; and comedy, improvisational, mime, and puppet shows and (2) establishments, commonly known as dinner theaters, engaged in producing live theatrical productions and in providing food and beverages for consumption on the premises. Theater groups or companies may or may not operate their own theater or other facility for staging their shows.

types.label: Fabric Mills
types.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in one of the following: (1) weaving broadwoven fabrics and felts (except tire fabrics and rugs); (2) weaving or braiding narrow fabrics; (3) making fabric-covered elastic yarn and thread; (4) manufacturing Schiffli machine embroideries; (5) manufacturing nonwoven fabrics and felts; (6) knitting weft (i.e., circular) and warp (i.e., flat) fabric; (7) knitting and finishing weft and warp fabric; (8) manufacturing lace; or (9) manufacturing, dyeing, and finishing lace and lace goods.

types.label: Drugs and Druggists' Sundries Merchant Wholesalers
Voluntary Health Organizations
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in raising funds for health related research, such as disease (e.g., heart, cancer, diabetes) prevention, health education, and patient services.

types.label: Audio and Video Equipment Manufacturing
types.definition: See industry description for 334310.

types.label: Goat Farming
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in raising goats.

types.label: Rendering and Meat Byproduct Processing
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in rendering animal fat, bones, and meat scraps.

types.label: Nursery and Tree Production
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in (1) growing nursery products, nursery stock, shrubbery, bulbs, fruit stock, sod, and so forth, under cover or in open fields and/or (2) growing short rotation woody trees with a growth and harvest cycle of 10 years or less for pulp or tree stock.

types.label: Supermarkets and Other Grocery Retailers (except Convenience Retailers)
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments generally known as supermarkets and other grocery retailers (except convenience retailers) primarily engaged in retailing a general line of food, such as canned and frozen foods; fresh fruits and vegetables; and fresh and prepared meats, fish, and poultry. Included in this industry are delicatessen-type establishments primarily engaged in retailing a general line of food.

types.label: Pulp Mills
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing pulp without manufacturing paper or paperboard. The pulp is made by separating the cellulose fibers from the other impurities in wood or other materials, such as used or recycled rags, linters, scrap paper, and straw.

types.label: Pharmaceutical and Medicine Manufacturing
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in one or more of the following: (1) manufacturing biological and medicinal products; (2) processing (i.e., grading, grinding, and milling) botanical drugs and herbs; (3) isolating active medicinal principals from botanical drugs and herbs; and (4) manufacturing pharmaceutical products intended for internal and external consumption in such forms as ampoules, tablets, capsules, vials, ointments, powders, solutions, and suspensions.

types.label: Engineered Wood Member Manufacturing
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing fabricated or laminated wood arches, wood roof and floor trusses, and/or other fabricated or laminated wood structural members.

types.label: General Line Grocery Merchant Wholesalers
types.definition: See industry description for 424410.

types.label: Spectator Sports
types.definition: This industry comprises (1) sports teams or clubs primarily participating in live sporting events before a paying audience; (2) establishments primarily engaged in operating racetracks without casinos; (3) independent athletes engaged in participating in live sporting or racing events before a paying audience; (4) owners of racing participants, such as cars, dogs, and horses, primarily engaged in entering them in racing events or other spectator sports events; and (5) establishments, such as sports trainers, primarily engaged in providing specialized services to support participants in sports events or competitions.  The sports teams and clubs included in this industry may or may not operate their own arena, stadium, or other facility for presenting their games or other spectator sports events.

types.label: Pulp Mills
types.definition: See industry description for 322110.

types.label: Scenic and Sightseeing Transportation, Land
types.definition: See industry description for 487110.

types.label: Food Service Contractors
