types.label: Fiduciary Relationship
types.definition: A fiduciary relationship is a legal relationship in which one party is entrusted with the care and management of another party's assets or interests, and is obligated to act in the best interests of the other party, with loyalty, honesty, and good faith.

types.label: payable_by_cl_name
types.definition:
"The name of the party paying the invoice.  May not be the same party that is paying VAT on the invoice.  

The legal name of the party paying the invoice may also be different from the CLIENT.cl_name, the INVOICE tax_invoice_cl_name and the INVOICE.bill_to_cl_name.  In some jurisdictions it may be required by law to provide this information.
"

types.label: Information Management Risk
types.definition: The threats and opportunities associated with an organization's capacity and sustainability of information management procedures and practices — including the potential for negative outcomes resulting from an organization's inability to effectively collect, store, process, and protect its data and information assets. This can stem from poor data quality, outdated systems, inadequate data security measures, or noncompliance with data protection regulations, potentially leading to data breaches, or legal liabilities, ultimately affecting the organization's performance.

types.label: Expungement
types.definition: Expungement is the legal process through which an arrest or conviction is removed from an individual's criminal record, effectively sealing or erasing it from public view. Once expunged, the individual typically does not need to disclose the arrest or conviction in most situations, such as during employment background checks, and it is as though the event never occurred in the eyes of the law.

types.label: Medical Negligence Claims
types.definition: Medical Negligence Claims refer to legal claims made by individuals who have suffered harm or injury due to the failure of medical professionals to provide an appropriate standard of care.

types.label: Motion to Introduce Evidence
types.definition: A Motion to Introduce Evidence is a formal request made to a court to allow the presentation of evidence during a trial or hearing.

types.label: Full-Time Employee
types.definition: A Full-Time Employee is an individual who works a minimum number of hours specified by their employer or by labor laws, often at least 35 to 40 hours per week. This classification usually comes with benefits such as health insurance, paid time off, and retirement plans, which may not be available to part-time or contract workers

types.label: Notice of Bankruptcy
types.definition: A Notice of Bankruptcy is a formal written communication that informs creditors and other interested parties that an individual or entity has filed for bankruptcy protection.

types.label: Crohn's Disease
types.definition: Crohn's disease is a chronic inflammatory condition of the gastrointestinal (GI) tract, which can affect any part from the mouth to the anus, though it most commonly impacts the small intestine and colon. The disease is characterized by transmural inflammation, which can lead to complications such as strictures, fistulas, and abscesses, and typically requires ongoing medical management and sometimes surgical intervention.

types.label: Nature of Work Clause
types.definition: A Nature of Work Clause is a provision in a contract that defines the type of work that will be performed by one or both parties involved in the agreement.

types.label: Note-Related Agreement
types.definition: A "Note-Related Agreement" is a supplementary or associated contract that clarifies, modifies, or elaborates upon the terms of a primary promissory note or similar debt instrument. This document may cover issues such as security interests, covenants, or guaranties that are not detailed in the main note but are critical to the lending arrangement.

types.label: Judicial Finding of Fact
types.definition: Finding of fact as adopted by a decisionmaker (e.g., judge, magistrate, arbitrator).

types.label: Entertainment Visa
types.definition: The Entertainment Visa (in the U.S., P-1B Visa), is designed for members of internationally recognized entertainment groups that wish to perform in the destination country (e.g., U.S.). In the United States, this non-immigrant visa allows the entertainers to stay for the duration of the event, competition, or performance, with an initial period of up to one year, which can be extended in increments of up to one year for continued performances or events

types.label: Motions for Bail
types.definition: A Motion for Bail is a formal request made to a court by a defendant or their attorney, asking for the release of the defendant from custody pending trial or appeal.

types.label: credit_note
types.definition:
"In the European Union (and possibly in other areas of the world) it is required to indicate whether an instrument is a Credit Note if it corrects a Tax Invoice.  
"

types.label: 450 Commerce (PACER NoS)
types.definition: Action filed under the Interstate Commerce Acts 49:1 et seq., 49:301

types.label: Transcript Appendix
types.definition: A transcript appendix is a supplementary section of a document that includes a written or recorded record of spoken words, typically used in legal proceedings.

types.label: New York District Court
types.definition: The New York District Court is a trial court within the New York State Courts system, with jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases in a specific geographic area within the state.

types.label: Deportation
types.definition: The forced removal of a person from a country by the government as a consequence of violating immigration laws or committing a crime.

types.label: Disinterested
types.definition: The attribute "disinterested" refers to parties, often trustees or professionals, who have no personal interest in the outcome of the proceedings and no prior relationship with the debtor or creditors. Disinterested parties ensure unbiased administration and decision-making, fostering fairness and integrity in the process.

types.label: Expired Parking Violation
types.definition: This occurs when a vehicle is parked in a regulated space beyond the time limit indicated on a parking meter or permit. The violation is typically enforced through a citation and fine issued by parking enforcement officers.

types.label: Meal Break
types.definition: A "Meal Break" is a period of time during the workday, typically lasting 30 minutes to an hour, in which employees are allowed to stop working and have a meal. This break is often unpaid and is intended to provide employees with the opportunity to eat and recharge.

types.label: Conflict of Interest Clause
types.definition: A Conflict of Interest Clause is a provision in a contract that requires the parties involved to disclose any potential conflicts of interest that may arise during the course of their relationship.

types.label: School Liability Claims
types.definition: School Liability Claims: Legal claims brought against educational institutions for damages or injuries caused by the institution's negligence or failure to provide a safe environment for students.

types.label: Claim Construction Brief
types.definition: A Claim Construction (Markman) Brief is a written document submitted to a court that provides an interpretation of the language used in patent claims, specifically for the purpose of determining the scope of the patent.

types.label: Bronchiectasis
types.definition: Bronchiectasis is a chronic respiratory condition characterized by abnormal and permanent dilation of the bronchial tubes, leading to impaired mucus clearance, chronic cough, and frequent respiratory infections. This condition results from damage to the airway walls, which can be caused by a variety of factors, including infections, genetic disorders, and autoimmune diseases.

types.label: Negative Commerce Clause Claim
types.definition: A Negative Commerce Clause claim is a legal argument asserting that a state law or regulation violates the United States Constitution by unduly burdening or discriminating against interstate commerce, even in the absence of federal legislation. This claim is based on the interpretation that the Negative Commerce Clause prohibits states from imposing unreasonable barriers on interstate trade and commerce, thereby ensuring a free and fair flow of goods and services between states.

types.label: Blacklisting Claim
types.definition: A blacklisting claim refers to a legal action taken by an individual or entity who alleges they have been unfairly prevented from obtaining employment, services, or opportunities due to being placed on a "blacklist." A blacklist is an unofficial list of persons or entities that are deemed undesirable or untrustworthy, resulting in exclusion from certain opportunities or associations.

types.label: Forfeiture Clause
types.definition: A forfeiture clause is a provision in a contract that allows one party to forfeit or lose their right to something, such as a deposit, if they fail to meet certain obligations outlined in the contract.

types.label: Jury Selection / Voire Dire Practice
types.definition: Jury Selection / Voire Dire Practice refers to the process of selecting a jury for a trial, which involves questioning potential jurors to determine their suitability for serving on the jury.

types.label: Medical Malpractice
types.definition: Medical Malpractice: Negligence or breach of duty by a healthcare professional that results in harm or injury to a patient.

types.label: Service Open
types.definition: The process is active.

types.label: Motion for Leave to Appeal
types.definition: A Motion for Leave to Appeal is a formal request made by a non-party filer in a bankruptcy case to seek permission from the court to appeal a decision made by a lower court.

types.label: Presumption of Innocence
types.definition: The presumption of innocence is a fundamental principle of criminal law that assumes an accused person is innocent until proven guilty. This cornerstone of the justice system places the burden of proof on the prosecution, requiring them to present sufficient evidence to convince a judge or jury of the defendant's guilt, and helps ensure that individuals are not unfairly convicted without proper evidence or due process.

types.label: Criminal Claim Degree
types.definition: The Criminal Claim Degree (Severity) refers to the level of seriousness of a criminal offense, such as a felony, misdemeanor, or infraction, within the context of a legal claim or litigation.

types.label: Georgia District Court - Bryan County
types.definition: Georgia District Court - Bryan County: A court of law in the state of Georgia that has jurisdiction over legal cases and disputes specifically within Bryan County.

types.label: Hair Evidence
types.definition: Hair evidence includes strands or fragments of hair found at crime scenes or on objects. Through microscopic examination and DNA analysis, hair can reveal information about its origin, potentially linking individuals to a particular location or event.

types.label: Entrapment
types.definition: Entrapment is a defense in criminal law where the defendant argues that law enforcement induced them to commit a crime they would not have otherwise committed. This defense is used to prevent the conviction of individuals who were coerced into illegal activities by police or government agents.

types.label: Exclusive Agreement Clause
types.definition: An exclusive agreement clause is a provision in a contract that restricts one or both parties from entering into similar agreements with other parties during the term of the contract.

types.label: Lovelock Paiute Tribe of the Lovelock Indian Colony, Nevada
INVOICE_CURRENCY
types.definition: The concept of INVOICE_CURRENCY refers to the specific currency used in a legal invoice, as defined by the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard.

types.label: Employee Re-Hire Event
types.definition: An Employee Re-Hire Event refers to the occasion when a former employee is formally rehired and rejoins the same organization. This event often involves the signing of a new employment contract and may necessitate another round of onboarding, while also potentially impacting seniority, benefits, and other employment conditions.

types.label: Collateral Estoppel
types.definition: Collateral Estoppel is a legal doctrine that prevents a party from relitigating an issue that has already been decided in a previous case, even if the parties and legal theories are different.

types.label: Contact City
types.definition: Contact City refers to the city where a person or entity can be reached and is a subcategory of Contact Information in the context of Engagement Terms for providing legal services.

types.label: Dependent Personality Disorder
types.definition: Dependent Personality Disorder is characterized by a pervasive and excessive need to be taken care of, leading to submissive and clinging behaviors and fears of separation. Individuals with this disorder have difficulty making independent decisions and rely heavily on others for emotional and practical support.

types.label: A111 Other
types.definition: A111 Other refers to an unspecified activity within the legal domain that does not fit into any other predefined category.

types.label: Prisoner Reentry
types.definition: Prisoner reentry refers to the process of individuals reintegrating into society after serving time in prison. It involves addressing various challenges such as employment, housing, and support services to reduce the likelihood of recidivism and help former prisoners successfully transition back into their communities.

types.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Crawford County (2nd Circuit Court)
Employment Misclassification Claim
types.definition: An employment misclassification claim is a legal action initiated by an employee who alleges that their employer has improperly classified them as an independent contractor, rather than an employee. The claim typically arises when an employer misclassifies an employee to avoid providing benefits or complying with certain employment laws, such as minimum wage and overtime requirements. Employees who are misclassified may be entitled to back wages, benefits, and other compensation.

types.label: 446 Americans With Disabilities - Other (PACER NoS)
types.definition: Action of discrimination against an individual with disabilities in areas other than employment, filed under 42 U.S.C. § 12133 (exclusion or discrimination in provision of services, programs or activities of a public entity) or 42 U.S.C. § 12188 (public accommodations)

types.label: Some Evidence
types.definition: Some Evidence refers to any type of proof or information presented in a legal case that supports one party's argument or position, and falls under the burden of proof required in litigation.

types.label: White Mountain Apache Tribe of the Fort Apache Reservation, Arizona
Employment Mandatory Training
types.definition: Employment Mandatory Training is a compulsory educational program required by an employer to address specific skills, knowledge gaps, or compliance issues among employees. This training aims to improve performance, ensure adherence to company policies, or meet legal and regulatory requirements.

types.label: Wildlife Crimes
types.definition: Wildlife Crimes involve illegal activities that harm wildlife species, including poaching, trafficking, and illegal trade. These crimes violate national and international laws aimed at protecting endangered and protected species.

types.label: New York Civil Court - New York County
types.definition: A court located in New York County that handles civil legal matters.

types.label: Assignment of Contract Clause
types.definition: The Assignment of Contract Clause is a provision in a contract that allows one party to transfer their rights and obligations to another party, typically for consideration.

types.label: Indiana Superior Court - Jay County
types.definition: The Indiana Superior Court - Jay County is a specific court within the Indiana Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over cases within Jay County, Indiana.

types.label: Standard of Performance Clause
types.definition: A Standard of Performance Clause is a provision in a contract that sets a specific level of performance or quality that must be met by one or both parties involved in the agreement.

types.label: Security Agreement
types.definition: A "Security Agreement" is a legal contract between a debtor and a secured party that outlines the collateral provided by the debtor to secure a loan or other obligation. The agreement defines the terms under which the secured party can take possession of the collateral in the event the debtor defaults.

types.label: Tuition Reimbursement
types.definition: Tuition reimbursement refers to a company benefit in which an employer pays back employees for the costs associated with furthering their education, typically for courses or degree programs that are relevant to their current or potential future roles within the company. This benefit often has specific terms, such as grade requirements or staying with the company for a certain period after course completion.

types.label: Failure to Provide Notice
types.definition: The failure of a party to provide proper notification or warning as required by law or contract, which may be used as a defense in civil litigation.

types.label: oasis:role collection
types.definition: A collection of roles defined by the Organization for the Advancement of Structured Information Standards (OASIS), which is a subset of a larger collection.

types.label: Telephone Consumer Protection Act Claim
types.definition: A Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) Claim is a legal claim made under the TCPA statute, which prohibits certain telemarketing practices and provides consumers with certain rights related to unwanted phone calls and text messages.

types.label: Outperformance Certificate
altLabels: An Outperformance Certificate, also known as a Leveraged ETF, is a financial instrument that allows disproportionate participation in the positive performance of the underlying asset(s) above a certain strike level. These certificates reflect the underlying price movements 1:1, adjusted by the conversion ratio and any related fees, offering a risk profile comparable to direct investment in the underlying asset(s) but with enhanced potential returns in favorable market conditions.

types.label: Joint and Several Liability
types.definition: Joint and Several Liability is a legal concept where multiple parties can be held responsible for the same damages or debt, and each party can be held liable for the entire amount.

types.label: Motion to Hear Case with Other Case
types.definition: A Motion to Hear Case with Other Case is a formal request made in appellate courts to consolidate two or more cases for hearing together.

types.label: Livestock Farmland
types.definition: Livestock Farmland pertains to designated agricultural areas used for rearing animals. Legal issues often concern animal welfare laws, property rights, leasing agreements, and related environmental regulations.

types.label: Failure to Accommodate
types.definition: A claim of failure to accommodate is a legal action taken by an individual, often an employee, alleging that their employer has not made reasonable adjustments or provided necessary support to allow them to perform their job effectively despite having a known disability, religious belief, or other protected characteristic. Employers are required by law, such as the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, to provide reasonable accommodations for employees with disabilities or religious beliefs, as long as doing so does not cause undue hardship to the employer.

types.label: Student's Dependent Visa
types.definition: A Student's Dependent Visa is a specialized visa category that allows the spouse and dependent children of a student visa holder to accompany them to the host country while they pursue their studies. Depending on the country's immigration policies, dependents may be allowed to work or study to a limited extent, but the primary purpose of their stay is to reside with the student visa holder.

types.label: Secrecy
types.definition: The concept of Secrecy refers to the legal defense strategy of withholding information or evidence from the opposing party in a legal matter, typically to protect confidential or privileged information.

types.label: Bladder Cancer
altLabels: Bladder cancer is a type of cancer that starts in the cells of the bladder, the organ responsible for storing urine. It often presents with symptoms such as blood in the urine and requires treatments including surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and immunotherapy.

types.label: oasis:Right
types.definition: A right, as defined in the OASIS ontology, is a type of deontic specification.

types.label: Rules of the Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation
types.definition: U.S. federal courts' body of procedural rules governing Multidistrict Litigation (MDLs).

types.label: Annelids
types.definition: Annelids are a phylum of invertebrate animals known as Annelida, characterized by their segmented bodies and a true coelom, which acts as a hydrostatic skeleton. This group includes earthworms, leeches, and polychaetes, and they play vital roles in soil aeration and aquatic ecosystems.

types.label: Common Carrier
types.definition: A common carrier is an individual or business that advertises to the public to transport people, offer goods, or provide services to the public. Common carriers are legally obligated to provide services to any paying customer without discrimination.

types.label: Viejas (Baron Long) Group of the Capitan Grande Band
Georgia Magistrate Court - Lowndes County
types.definition: A court in Lowndes County, Georgia that has limited jurisdiction over certain civil and criminal cases.

types.label: NATO-3 Visa
altLabels: International Military Alliance Clerical Staff Visa
types.definition: A NATO-3 visa is issued to official clerical staff accompanying a NATO-1 visa holder, allowing them to enter the U.S. to perform their duties. This visa category includes support staff essential for the operation of NATO-1 personnel.

types.label: Visa for Temporary Non-Agricultural Workers
types.definition: A Temporary Non-Agricultural Workers Visa, such as the U.S. H-2B Visa, is a category of visa that permits foreign nationals to work temporarily in non-agricultural sectors of a host country. This type of visa is often used to fill temporary labor shortages in industries such as hospitality, construction, landscaping, or seasonal businesses.

types.label: Adjustment of Status Pending
altLabels: In immigration law, "Adjustment of Status Pending" refers to the interim period during which an individual's application to adjust their immigration status, often from a non-immigrant to an immigrant status (permanent resident), is under review by the immigration authorities (e.g., U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS)). During this time, the applicant is generally authorized to remain in the destination country (e.g., U.S.) and may be eligible for work authorization and other interim benefits while awaiting a final decision

types.label: Unlimited Ruleset
types.definition: A set of rules that applies to all cases within a particular jurisdiction, without any limitations or exceptions.

types.label: Warehousing and Storage Industry
types.definition: Industries in this group are primarily engaged in operating warehousing and storage facilities for general merchandise, refrigerated goods, and other warehouse products. These establishments provide facilities to store goods. They do not sell the goods they handle. These establishments take responsibility for storing the goods and keeping them secure. They may also provide a range of services, often referred to as logistics services, related to the distribution of goods. Logistics services can include labeling, breaking bulk, inventory control and management, light assembly, order entry and fulfillment, packaging, pick and pack, price marking and ticketing, and transportation arrangement. However, establishments in this industry group always provide warehousing or storage services in addition to any logistic services. Furthermore, the warehousing or storage of goods must be more than incidental to the performance of services, such as price marking.

types.label: Standalone Material Adverse Effect Closing Condition
types.definition: A Standalone Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Closing Condition, also known as MAE, is a specific language used in legal agreements that outlines the circumstances under which a party can terminate the agreement due to a significant negative change in the financial or operational condition of the other party.

types.label: Human Resources Management Risk
types.definition: The threats and opportunities associated with staff/management turnover; employment/work culture; recruitment, retention and staffing processes and practices; succession planning and talent management; and employee development, training, and capacity building. It also includes the potential for negative consequences arising from an organization's ineffective or inefficient handling of its workforce-related policies, practices, and processes. This can result from poor recruitment, inadequate training, weak retention strategies, or insufficient attention to employee satisfaction and development, potentially leading to reduced productivity, and increased turnover, ultimately impacting the organization's overall performance.

types.label: Foster Care Negligence
types.definition: Negligent actions or omissions by parents that result in harm or injury to a child who has been placed in foster care.

types.label: California Family Rights Act Claim
types.definition: A California Family Rights Act (CFRA) claim is a legal action initiated by an employee against their employer for not complying with the CFRA, which provides eligible employees with up to 12 weeks of unpaid leave in a 12-month period for certain family or medical reasons, such as the birth or adoption of a child, the employee's own serious health condition, or to care for a seriously ill family member. The claim typically arises when an employer denies an employee's request for CFRA leave or interferes with an employee's right to take CFRA leave, or retaliates against an employee for exercising their right to CFRA leave. Employers can face liability for violating the CFRA, which can result in significant damages for the affected employee.

types.label: Debt Supplemental Agreement
types.definition: A Debt Supplemental Agreement is an addendum or modification to an existing debt agreement or indenture. It serves to amend, clarify, or add new terms and conditions to the original contract, such as changing the interest rate, extending the repayment schedule, or adding covenants, without altering the fundamental nature of the initial agreement.

types.label: Remote Synchronous Communication
types.definition: A communication that occurs synchronously and remotely, such as a telephone call or videoconference (e.g., Zoom, Teams, Meet).

types.label: Hidden Assets Claim
types.definition: A Hidden Assets Claim is a legal action taken during divorce proceedings when one spouse suspects that the other spouse is concealing or not fully disclosing assets or financial information. This claim seeks to uncover any undisclosed or hidden assets, which could include bank accounts, investments, real estate, or other valuable property, to ensure a fair and accurate division of marital property during the divorce process. Discovery methods and legal processes are used to identify and reveal any concealed assets.

types.label: Probate Reason of Financial Exploitation
types.definition: Probate Reason of Financial Exploitation: A legal cause for initiating a probate filing due to the suspected or proven financial exploitation of a deceased person.

types.label: Florida Circuit Court - Bay County - 14th Circuit Court
types.definition: A court located in Bay County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system.

types.label: Air Quality Rights
types.definition: Air Quality Rights refer to the legal entitlements and standards established to ensure the purity and safety of the air we breathe. This encompasses the right of individuals and communities to access clean and unpolluted air and places regulatory obligations on governments and industries to limit emissions, control pollutants, and maintain air quality standards to safeguard public health and the environment.

types.label: Data Privacy Clause
types.definition: A Data Privacy Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the obligations and rights of parties with respect to the collection, use, and protection of personal data.

types.label: Caudal Regression Syndrome
types.definition: Caudal Regression Syndrome (CRS) is a rare congenital disorder that results from abnormal development of the lower spine and structures. It affects the development of the caudal (tail) region of the embryo, leading to a spectrum of anomalies involving the lower spinal cord, pelvis, and lower limbs.

types.label: United Nations
types.definition: The United Nations (UN) is an international organization founded in 1945 to promote peace, security, and cooperation among member states. It aims to address global challenges such as poverty, climate change, and conflict, and provides a forum for countries to engage in diplomatic relations and collective decision-making.

types.label: Public Intoxication
types.definition: To drink alcoholic beverages to the extent that one’s mental faculties and physical coordination are substantially impaired.

types.label: Hedge Fund
types.definition: A hedge fund is a type of investment vehicle that pools capital from accredited individuals or institutional investors and invests in a variety of assets, often using complex strategies with the goal of generating high returns. Unlike mutual funds, hedge funds are subject to fewer regulations and often employ more aggressive strategies, including short selling, leverage, and derivatives.

types.label: "Material Adverse Effect" Definition - Exceptions - Failure to Meet Projections
Stakeholders and Partnerships Risk
types.definition: The threats and opportunities associated with an organization's partners and stakeholder demographics, characteristics, and activities. This includes the potential for negative consequences arising from an organization's inability to effectively manage relationships with key stakeholders, such as customers, suppliers, investors, or partners. Causes can include poor communication, misaligned expectations, or unaddressed concerns, potentially leading to diminished trust, reduced collaboration, or loss of support, ultimately impacting the organization's overall performance, reputation, and growth opportunities

types.label: Intentional Interference with Prospective Economic Advantage
types.definition: Intentional Interference with Prospective Economic Advantage refers to a tort where a third party intentionally disrupts a business relationship or contract between two parties, causing economic harm to one of the parties.

types.label: "Material Adverse Effect" Definition - Exceptions - Acts of War
Limited Liability Partnership
types.definition: A limited liability partnership (LLP) is a partnership in which some or all partners (depending on the jurisdiction) have limited liabilities. It therefore can exhibit elements of partnerships and corporations. In a LLP, each partner is not responsible or liable for another partner's misconduct or negligence.

types.label: Georgia Superior Court - Henry County
types.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Henry County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Henry County.

types.label: Georgia Superior Court - Colquitt County
types.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Colquitt County.

types.label: Board of Directors
types.definition: The board of directors for a legal entity (e.g., corporation, nonprofit).

types.label: Fee Objection Practice
types.definition: Fee Objection Practice (Bankruptcy) refers to the legal practice area that deals with objections to fees charged by professionals in bankruptcy cases.

types.label: Bankruptcy Budgeting Practice
types.definition: Developing strategy for — and preparing — a debtor's Operating Reports (e.g., Budget Preparation, Budget Updates).

types.label: Estoppel Letters Clause
types.definition: A clause in a contract that prevents a party from denying certain facts or legal rights that have already been established or agreed upon in a previous communication.

types.label: Drivers Privacy Protection Act Claim
types.definition: A Drivers Privacy Protection Act Claim is a legal claim that arises from the violation of the federal law that regulates the disclosure of personal information contained in motor vehicle records.

types.label: Melanoma
types.definition: Melanoma is a type of skin cancer that develops from the pigment-producing cells known as melanocytes. It is considered the most dangerous form of skin cancer due to its ability to spread to other parts of the body if not detected early, requiring treatments such as surgery, immunotherapy, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy.

types.label: Investigation Practice
types.definition: An investigation, search, or examination with an intention to discover facts and their relationship to law.

types.label: Generic Matter Narrative
types.definition: A generic version of a matter narrative. Usually used to further describe a category of matters.

types.label: Assisted Suicide
types.definition: Assisted Suicide: The act of intentionally helping another person end their life, typically in cases where the person is suffering from a terminal illness or severe pain, and where the person has expressed a desire to die.

types.label: Kansas District Court - Woodson County
types.definition: A court located in Woodson County, Kansas that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

types.label: Georgia Superior Court - Marion County
types.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Marion County is a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Marion County.

types.label: Sales and Consumption Tax Payment
altLabels: Tax payment on production, sale, transfer, leasing and delivery of goods and rendering of services
types.definition: Sales and Consumption Tax Payment (aka Tax payment on production, sale, transfer, leasing and delivery of goods and rendering of services) consists of all taxes, levied on transactions in goods and services on the basis of their intrinsic characteristics (e.g., value, weight of tobacco, strength of alcohol, and so on) as distinct from taxes imposed on the use of goods, or permission to use goods or perform activities.

types.label: Solar Energy Law
types.definition: Laws pertaining to solar power.

types.label: Eviction (Event)
types.definition: Eviction is a legal process by which a landlord forces a tenant to leave a rented property, typically due to nonpayment of rent, lease violations, or other breaches of the rental agreement. The process involves court proceedings, notice requirements, and, if ordered by the court, law enforcement intervention to remove the tenant from the property.

types.label: Lemons
types.definition: Lemons are small, yellow citrus fruits from the Citrus limon species, known for their tart, acidic juice and aromatic zest. They are widely used in culinary applications, beverages, and as a natural cleaning agent, valued for their high vitamin C content and refreshing flavor.

types.label: Identification of Documents Practice
types.definition: Identification of Documents Practice refers to the process of locating and selecting relevant documents for a legal matter, which is a subset of the broader Document Collection and Production Practice.

types.label: Inappropriate Content
types.definition: Inappropriate Content refers to claim regarding material that is deemed offensive, objectionable, or unsuitable for certain audiences, often violating societal norms or legal standards. This can include offensive language, explicit material, or any content that is considered harmful or inappropriate for public display or consumption.

types.label: Citation to Legal Authority
types.definition: A document's citations to legal authorities (e.g., cases, statutes, regulations).

types.label: Voter Fraud Claim
types.definition: A Voter Fraud Claim refers to an allegation that illegal actions were taken to manipulate the outcome of an election, including activities such as voting more than once, casting ballots under false identities, tampering with vote counts, or falsifying voter registrations. These claims question the integrity of the voting process and require investigation to ensure electoral fairness.

types.label: Hospice Negligence
types.definition: Hospice Negligence refers to a legal claim for damages resulting from the failure of a hospice provider to provide adequate care and treatment to a patient who is terminally ill or in need of end-of-life care.

types.label: Collection Limitation Principle
types.definition: Collection Limitation is the privacy principle that there should be limits to the collection of personal data and any such data should be obtained by lawful and fair means and, where appropriate, with the knowledge or consent of the data subject

types.label: First Amendment Defense
types.definition: A First Amendment Defense is a legal strategy used in both criminal and civil litigation to protect an individual's right to free speech, religion, press, assembly, and petition as guaranteed by the First Amendment of the United States Constitution.

types.label: Stop Sign Violation Claim
types.definition: A Stop Sign Violation Claim involves a legal allegation that a driver has failed to make a complete stop at a stop sign as required by traffic regulations, potentially leading to administrative or legal penalties. Such claims are integral to traffic law enforcement and often necessitate evidence review and legal proceedings to resolve.

types.label: Petition for Visa for Dependent of Intended Spouse of Citizen
types.definition: In the United States, a "Petition for Alien Fiancé(e)" refers to Form I-129F in the United States, which is used by U.S. citizens to petition for their foreign fiancé(e) to enter the U.S. for the purpose of getting married. This form initiates the K-1 visa process, allowing the foreign fiancé(e) to travel to the U.S. and marry the U.S. citizen petitioner within 90 days of arrival

types.label: Reletting Clause
types.definition: A reletting clause is a provision in a contract that allows the landlord to lease the property to a new tenant if the original tenant breaches the lease agreement.

types.label: Business Unit
types.definition: A Business Unit is a distinct division or department within an organization that operates with specific objectives and a degree of autonomy. It is often responsible for its own profit and loss, strategy, and operations, allowing it to be evaluated independently for performance and contribution to the overall corporate goals

types.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Henry County 2
types.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Henry County, Indiana, with the authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

types.label: Mississippi Ethics Opinions
types.definition: Mississippi Ethics Opinions are official statements issued by the Mississippi State Courts that provide guidance on ethical issues faced by attorneys and judges in the state of Mississippi.

types.label: Persian
types.definition: Persian (Language) is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a member of the Language class, used in legal matters.

types.label: Non-current Law
types.definition: The previously effective law currently appears to have no legal efficacy, having been displaced (e.g., overruled, reversed, vacated, superseded).

types.label: Normal Rate Dividend Payment
types.definition: Normal Rate Income refers to a type of dividend income where shareholders receive the same dividends as common or ordinary shareholders but have additional privileges, such as preferential treatment in the distribution of assets upon the company's dissolution. These shareholders benefit from regular dividend payments while retaining certain priority rights in specific circumstances.

types.label: Crimean Tatar; Crimean Turkish
types.definition: A language spoken by the Crimean Tatar people, primarily in Crimea and Turkey.

types.label: Litigation Support Vendors Expense
types.definition: Expenses incurred by vendors who provide support services to parties involved in a legal dispute, such as document management, e-discovery, and trial presentation services.

types.label: Organic Products Market Segment
types.definition: The organic foods market segment refers to a division of the market that is specifically targeted towards consumers who are interested in foods that are produced using methods that do not involve synthetic pesticides, fertilizers, genetically modified organisms (GMOs), or irradiation. This segment encompasses products and marketing strategies that are designed to cater to the needs, preferences, and interests of individuals who seek natural, environmentally friendly, and health-conscious food options.

types.label: Grandparent
types.definition: A Grandparent is an individual who is the parent of one's mother or father. They are one generation removed from the primary familial lineage, and their children are typically referred to as the aunts or uncles of the subsequent generation.

types.label: Arawak
types.definition: Arawak (Language) is a structured system of communication spoken by the Arawak people, characterized by its own grammar and vocabulary, and is a subcategory of the Language top-level class.

types.label: Pension Account
types.definition: A pension account is a financial arrangement where an individual or employee contributes funds during their working years to build a retirement fund. The accumulated funds are invested, and upon retirement, the account provides regular payments or a lump sum to support the retiree's financial needs.

types.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Sherman County
types.definition: Oregon Circuit Court - Sherman County: A specific court within the Oregon Circuit Court system located in Sherman County, with jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

types.label: Post-Trial Submission Practice
types.definition: Post-Trial Submission Practice refers to the legal activities and procedures that take place after a trial has concluded, such as filing motions, briefs, and other documents with the court.

types.label: Minnesota District Court - Stevens County
types.definition: Minnesota District Court - Stevens County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system located in Stevens County, Minnesota.

types.label: ICC Arbitration Clause
types.definition: An ICC Arbitration Clause is a specific type of contractual clause that designates the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) as the arbitrator in the event of a dispute between parties to the contract.

types.label: New Jersey Superior Court - Middlesex County
types.definition: The New Jersey Superior Court - Middlesex County is a specific court within the New Jersey Superior Court Appellate Division that has jurisdiction over cases in Middlesex County.

types.label: Analysis of Student Loan Obligations
types.definition: An Analysis of Student Loan Obligations involves the review and assessment of student loan agreements and payment histories to determine their current status and implications for debtors, particularly in contexts like bankruptcy or repayment plan negotiations. This analysis helps determine the enforceability, priority, and potential for discharge or restructuring of student loan debts.

types.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Baker County
types.definition: Oregon Circuit Court - Baker County: A specific court within the Oregon Circuit Court system located in Baker County, with jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

types.label: California Court of Appeal - 6th Dist.
types.definition: The California Court of Appeal - 6th Dist. is a specific division of the California Court of Appeal that hears appeals from trial courts in the 6th district of California.

types.label: Analysis of Utilities Considerations
types.definition: Analysis of Utilities Considerations refers to the evaluation and assessment of the various utility factors involved in an obligation analysis.

types.label: Guardian Ad Litem Attorney
types.definition: A Guardian Ad Litem (GAL) Attorney is a type of lawyer who is appointed by the court to represent the best interests of a child or incapacitated adult in a legal proceeding.

types.label: Flax
types.definition: Flax is a fiber crop cultivated for its strong and durable fibers, used primarily to produce linen fabric. In addition to its textile applications, flax seeds are used to extract oil, known as linseed oil, which is utilized in various industrial and culinary applications.

types.label: Grazing Rights
types.definition: These grant an individual or entity the right to allow their livestock to feed (or graze) on specific areas of land. Often, these rights are leased or licensed by landowners or governmental entities.

types.label: Motion to Extend Time to Appeal
types.definition: A Motion to Extend Time to Appeal is a request made to a higher court to allow additional time beyond the deadline for filing an appeal, typically made by a party who missed the original deadline due to circumstances beyond their control.

types.label: Liver Transplantation
types.definition: Liver transplantation is a surgical procedure in which a diseased liver is replaced with a healthy donor liver to restore normal liver function. This procedure is typically performed for patients with end-stage liver disease, acute liver failure, or certain liver cancers, and requires lifelong immunosuppressive therapy to prevent organ rejection.

types.label: Mortgage Foreclosure
types.definition: The concept of Mortgage Foreclosure refers to the legal process by which a lender takes possession of a property when the borrower fails to make mortgage payments, and sells it to recover the outstanding debt.

types.label: Reseller Agreement
types.definition: A Reseller Agreement is a legal contract between a manufacturer or wholesaler and a reseller, outlining the terms and conditions of the resale of goods or services.

types.label: New York City Court - Little Falls
types.definition: A court located in Little Falls, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court system.

types.label: Motion to Strike Expert Reports
types.definition: A Motion to Strike Expert Reports is a legal request to exclude or remove expert reports from being presented as evidence in a trial or hearing.

types.label: Other Recurrent Use and Permission Tax Payment
types.definition: Other Recurrent Use and Permission Tax Payment covers taxes levied on a recurring basis for business and professional licenses required to carry on particular types of businesses or professions. This includes licenses such as those for taxis and casinos, as well as dog licenses and recurrent general licenses for hunting, shooting, and fishing. Broadcast license fees are included when the payer cannot opt out from making payments for public broadcasting, even if they do not consume such services. Specific exemptions do not alter the compulsory nature of these payments.

types.label: Non-criminal Traffic Violation
types.definition: A non-criminal traffic violation is a type of traffic violation claim that does not involve criminal charges or penalties.

types.label: Dating Market Segment
types.definition: The dating market refers to a division of the market that is specifically targeted towards individuals who are seeking romantic relationships. This segment encompasses products and services that facilitate the process of finding and connecting with potential partners, such as dating apps, matchmaking services, and social events.

types.label: Texas District Court - Medina County
types.definition: A Texas District Court located in Medina County, which has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

types.label: Khotanese; Sakan
types.definition: Khotanese and Sakan are languages that belong to the Language class and are used in legal matters as a means of communication.

types.label: JC20 Legal investigation (UK J-CODE)
types.definition: Includes identification of the legal issues raised by the case facts and developing the strategy for the case.

types.label: Debt Mutual Fund
types.definition: A Debt Mutual Fund is an investment vehicle that pools money from various investors to purchase a diversified portfolio of debt securities such as bonds, corporate debentures, and government securities. The fund aims to generate returns through interest income and capital appreciation, and it is generally considered lower risk compared to equity mutual funds.

types.label: Massachusetts Superior Court - Plymouth County
types.definition: The Massachusetts Superior Court - Plymouth County is a court of general jurisdiction in Massachusetts that hears civil and criminal cases within Plymouth County.

types.label: Request for Information
types.definition: Document where a buyer collects written information about the capabilities of various legal service providers, normally in a format that can be used to compare providers. In the context of immigration, an RFI refers to a formal communication from immigration authorities to an applicant, seeking additional documentation, clarification, or details to further assess the application.

types.label: Service of Process Event
types.definition: The Service of Process Event is a specific type of event within the context of litigation, which involves the delivery of legal documents to a party in a case.

types.label: Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court - Cameron County
types.definition: A Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court in Cameron County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Magisterial District Court system that has jurisdiction over minor criminal offenses and civil cases within its geographical area.

types.label: Common Law Copyright Infringement
types.definition: The unauthorized use or reproduction of a creative work protected under common law, which violates the exclusive rights of the owner and may result in legal action for damages or injunctions.

types.label: Psychotherapist-Patient Privilege
types.definition: A legal protection that allows a patient to keep confidential any communications made during psychotherapy sessions with their therapist.

types.label: Motion to Dissolve Temporary Restraining Order
types.definition: A Motion to Dissolve Temporary Restraining Order is a formal request made to the court to lift a temporary order that prohibits a party from taking certain actions until a hearing can be held to determine whether a permanent order should be issued.

types.label: Backup Certificate
types.definition: A Backup Certificate is a document certifying the accuracy and completeness of Legal Opinion's facts. Authors might include clients, law firms, or third parties. Backup certificates serve as a reassurance that the facts in the Legal Opinion are valid.

types.label: Substantive Unconscionability Permitting Contract Rescission
types.definition: A legal concept that refers to the presence of unfair or oppressive terms in a contract that allow for the contract to be cancelled or rescinded.

types.label: Analysis of Securities Reporting Considerations
types.definition: Analysis of Securities Reporting Considerations refers to the process of examining and evaluating the legal obligations and requirements related to the reporting of securities, including financial statements and other disclosures, in order to ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations.

types.label: Motion to Exclude Document
types.definition: A Motion to Exclude Document is a legal request made by a party in a case to prevent a specific document or evidence from being presented in court.

types.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas -  Perry County
types.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Perry County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in Perry County, Pennsylvania.

types.label: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services Industry
types.definition: The Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services subsector groups establishments that provide computing infrastructure, data processing services, Web hosting services (except software publishing), and related services, including streaming support services (except streaming distribution services).

types.label: Motion for Relief due to Clerical Error
types.definition: A Motion for Relief due to Clerical Error is a legal request to correct a mistake made by the court or court clerk in a previous order or judgment.

types.label: Total Amount - Expense
types.definition: Total, cumulative amount paid in expenses.

types.label: New York Supreme Court - Bronx County
types.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Bronx County is a court of general jurisdiction located in the Bronx borough of New York City.

types.label: School-Based Public Benefit
types.definition: A school-based public benefit refers to programs or services provided in educational institutions to support the well-being and education of students, particularly those from low-income backgrounds. Examples include school breakfast and lunch programs, as well as initiatives aimed at improving the educational opportunities and outcomes for disadvantaged students.

types.label: Lease Practice
types.definition: A contract by which one party (landlord, or lessor) gives to another (tenant, or lessee) the use and possession of lands, buildings, property, etc. for a specified time and for fixed payments.

types.label: Creek
types.definition: A Native American language spoken by the Creek people, primarily in the southeastern United States.

types.label: Sisal
types.definition: Sisal is a strong, durable natural fiber obtained from the leaves of the Agave sisalana plant, primarily used in the production of ropes, twines, and matting. Its resilience and versatility make it a preferred choice for agricultural, marine, and industrial applications.

types.label: Kansas District Court - Dickinson County
types.definition: Kansas District Court - Dickinson County refers to a specific court within the Kansas District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Dickinson County.

types.label: LAW_FIRM_ADDRESS_1
types.definition: The concept LAW_FIRM_ADDRESS_1 refers to the first line of the address of a law firm and is a component of the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard for electronic legal invoicing.

types.label: Negligent Hiring
types.definition: Negligent Hiring: A legal claim that arises when an employer fails to exercise reasonable care in hiring an employee, resulting in harm to a third party.

types.label: JB30 Budgeting - between the parties (UK J-CODE)
types.definition: Work on budgeting between the parties following initial completion of the first budget, including the monitoring of costs incurred against the budget and any applications for variation of a budget.

types.label: Responses to Requests for Admission
types.definition: Responses to Requests for Admission are written statements made in response to a request for admission, which is a type of discovery document used in legal proceedings to establish the truth of certain facts.

types.label: Consent in Lieu of Meeting Clause
types.definition: A Consent in Lieu of Meeting Clause is a provision in a contract that allows parties to give their consent to a proposed action without the need for a formal meeting.

types.label: AI Governance
types.definition: AI Governance refers to the frameworks, policies, and practices that guide the ethical development, deployment, and oversight of artificial intelligence systems. It encompasses the establishment of standards and regulations to ensure AI systems are transparent, accountable, and aligned with societal values and ethical principles

types.label: Freedom from War and Armed Conflict
types.definition: Freedom from war and armed conflict is a human aspiration often reflected in international humanitarian law, which seeks to limit the effects of armed conflict on people and communities. While not always explicitly defined as a "right," various international treaties like the Geneva Conventions aim to protect civilians, prisoners of war, and combatants from unnecessary suffering and violence during times of conflict.

types.label: Computer Malpractice
types.definition: Computer Malpractice refers to a type of malpractice claim that arises from the failure of a professional to use reasonable care in the use of computer technology, resulting in harm to a client or patient.

types.label: oasis:Expression
types.definition: A type of metadata that describes a work of art or literature, including its author, title, and other identifying information.

types.label: Diversity Jurisdiction
types.definition: The concept of Diversity Jurisdiction refers to the authority of a federal court to hear a case between parties from different states or countries, where the amount in controversy exceeds a certain threshold.

types.label: Neurology Malpractice
types.definition: Negligent or wrongful conduct by a medical professional in the field of neurology, resulting in harm or injury to a patient.

types.label: Peripheral Arterial Disease
types.definition: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a condition characterized by the narrowing or blockage of peripheral arteries, typically in the legs, due to atherosclerosis or other vascular issues. PAD can cause symptoms such as claudication (pain during walking), decreased limb perfusion, and can lead to severe complications including ulcers or gangrene if untreated.

types.label: Judicial Order
types.definition: A judicial order is a written directive issued by a court, typically in response to a motion or petition, that directs a party to take or refrain from taking a particular action.

types.label: Secret
types.definition: Secret is a security classification level used for information that requires significant protection because its unauthorized disclosure could cause serious damage to the organization (e.g., company, nonprofit, nation). Access to secret information is restricted to individuals with the appropriate security clearance and a demonstrated need to know.

types.label: Notice of Related Cases
types.definition: A Notice of Related Cases is a written communication informing parties involved in a legal case of other cases that may have a bearing on the current case.

types.label: Idaho Juvenile Court
types.definition: Idaho Juvenile Court refers to a specialized court within the Idaho State Courts system that deals with cases involving minors.

types.label: End-to-End Transaction Management
types.definition: End-to-End Transaction Management refers to the complete process of managing legal transactions from start to finish, including all necessary steps and parties involved.

types.label: Grand Jury Proceeding
types.definition: A Grand Jury Proceeding is a legal process where a group of citizens is convened to determine whether there is enough evidence to bring criminal charges against a person or entity.

types.label: Arkansas District Court - Independence Cty.
types.definition: Arkansas District Court - Independence Cty. is a specific court within the Arkansas District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Independence County, Arkansas.

types.label: Employer Retaliation
types.definition: The act of an employer taking adverse action against an employee in response to the employee engaging in protected activity, such as reporting illegal conduct or filing a workers' compensation claim.

types.label: Motion to Add Creditors
types.definition: A Motion to Add Creditors is a formal request filed in a bankruptcy case by the debtor to include additional creditors not originally listed in the initial bankruptcy schedules. This motion ensures that all relevant parties are notified of the bankruptcy proceedings and can participate in the distribution of assets or discharge of debts.

types.label: Business Trust
types.definition: A business trust is a form of business organization which is similar to a corporation, in which investors receive transferable certificates of beneficial interest.

types.label: New Mexico Metropolitan Court - Bernalillo County
types.definition: The New Mexico Metropolitan Court - Bernalillo County is a specific court within the New Mexico Metropolitan Court system that handles cases within Bernalillo County.

types.label: False Designation of Origin
types.definition: A False Designation of Origin claim may be filed when an entity falsely represents the origin of their goods or services, misleading consumers and potentially causing damage to the business or reputation of the rightful owner of the trademark. In the United States, this type of claim is typically brought under the Lanham Act.

types.label: Pechanga Band of Luiseno Mission Indians
Payment Defense
types.definition: A Payment Defense is a legal argument or strategy used by a defendant in a civil litigation case to refute or deny the plaintiff's claim for payment.

types.label: L200 Pre-Trial Pleadings and Motions
types.definition: L200 Pre-Trial Pleadings and Motions refer to the initial legal documents and requests filed by parties in a lawsuit before the trial phase, including complaints, answers, and motions.

types.label: Engagement Arrangements
types.definition: Ancillary engagement terms and features that the Provider may provide the Buyer, which may or may not involve remuneration.

types.label: Output VAT Payment
types.definition: Output VAT Payment refers to the Value Added Tax that a business collects on its sales of goods and services. This tax is remitted to the government after offsetting any Input VAT, ensuring businesses pay VAT only on the value they add to the products or services.

types.label: Shoshone-Bannock Tribes of the Fort Hall Reservation
Zoning Text Amendments
types.definition: Zoning Text Amendments refer to the changes made to the written regulations and ordinances that define how the land within different zones can be used. These changes can clarify ambiguities, address new development challenges, or enact new policies, and typically require legal review, public hearings, and governmental approvals.

types.label: Appellate Letter
types.definition: An appellate letter is a written communication submitted to a higher court requesting review of a lower court's decision, and is a type of correspondence and form used in the appellate filing process.

types.label: Business Division
types.definition: A Business Division is a large organizational unit within a company that operates somewhat independently, often with its own profit and loss responsibility. It typically focuses on a distinct product line or market segment and may contain multiple departments or business units to support its specific objectives and operations

types.label: Motion for Judgment on the Pleadings
types.definition: A Motion for Judgment on the Pleadings is a type of dispositive motion that asks the court to make a decision based solely on the pleadings and without the need for a trial.

types.label: INVOICE_TAX_TOTAL
types.definition: The concept of INVOICE_TAX_TOTAL refers to the total amount of taxes charged on an invoice, as defined in the LEDES98BI V5 Format Rev 1-2020 standard.

types.label: Transaction Negotiation Dynamics
types.definition: Transaction negotiation dynamics refer to the processes and interactions involved in negotiating the terms and conditions of a business transaction between parties. These dynamics encompass various strategies, styles, and behaviors that influence the negotiation's outcome, including the degree of cooperation, conflict, and communication between the parties involved.

types.label: Bankruptcy Schedule - Expenses
types.definition: Bankruptcy Schedule - Expenses, also known as Schedule J, requires the debtor to list all monthly living expenses, including housing, utilities, food, transportation, and other necessary costs. This schedule provides a detailed account of the debtor's expenditure, helping the court and creditors understand the debtor's financial obligations and capacity for debt repayment.

types.label: Visa for Specialty Occupation Workers from Australia
types.definition: The visa for Specialty Occupation Workers from Australia, commonly known as the E-3 visa in the United States, is a special work visa category that allows Australian nationals to work in a "specialty occupation" in the U.S. A "specialty occupation" is generally defined as a role requiring a bachelor's degree or higher in a specific field, and the visa is subject to annual numerical limitations.

types.label: Employment Geographic Location
types.definition: Employment Geographic Location refers to the physical or virtual place where an employee performs their job duties, which can range from a specific city, state, or country to a remote setting. This location often has implications for taxation, labor laws, and eligibility for location-based benefits or allowances.

types.label: Buyer Consent Not Unreasonably Withheld
types.definition: The concept of "Buyer Consent Not Unreasonably Withheld" refers to the requirement that a buyer's consent must be obtained before a certain action can be taken, but the buyer cannot unreasonably withhold their consent.

types.label: New York Civil Court - Queens County
types.definition: A court located in Queens County, New York that handles civil legal disputes within its jurisdiction.

types.label: Interference with Contractual Right
types.definition: The concept of Interference with Contractual Right refers to the intentional and unjustified interference with a contractual relationship between two parties by a third party, causing harm or damages to one of the parties involved.

types.label: Information Security Law
types.definition: Law regulating the protection of information and information systems from unauthorized access

types.label: Expert Witness Management
types.definition: Expert Witness Management refers to the process of managing and coordinating the selection, retention, and preparation of expert witnesses for use in legal proceedings, within the broader context of Litigation Management.

types.label: Zapotec
types.definition: Zapotec (Language) is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary specific to the Zapotec people and culture.

types.label: Matter Discount or Credit Category
types.definition: A Matter Discount or Credit Category is a subcategory of Discounts and Credits that pertains specifically to the reduction of fees or costs associated with a particular legal matter.

types.label: Wrongful Conviction
types.definition: A wrongful conviction is a legal concept that refers to the conviction of an innocent person due to errors or misconduct by the government, resulting in damages for which the government may be held liable under the legal theory of governmental tort liability.

types.label: Seller
types.definition: A seller is a person, company or entity who sells a thing or property in exchange for other property (often money). One who disposes of a thing in consideration of money.

types.label: Order for Remote Hearing
types.definition: An Order for Telephonic Hearing is a written document that directs a court proceeding to be conducted via telephone, videoconference, or other remote means, and is typically used in bankruptcy and restructuring cases.

types.label: Criminal Battery
types.definition: The intentional and unlawful use of force against another person, resulting in harmful or offensive contact, without that person's consent.

types.label: Civil Legal Determination
types.definition: A "civil legal determination" refers to the decision or verdict made by a court in a civil case. It includes outcomes such as finding a party liable or not liable for a particular claim or issue. This determination often leads to remedies or judgments, such as monetary awards or injunctive relief, to resolve the dispute between the parties involved in the civil litigation.

types.label: "'Reasonably likely/expected breach' of fiduciary duties" Language
types.definition: The concept of "'Reasonably likely/expected breach' of fiduciary duties" refers to the language used in legal documents to describe a situation where a fiduciary is expected to violate their duties, and the legal standards that apply in such a scenario.

types.label: Last Clear Chance Doctrine
types.definition: The Last Clear Chance Doctrine is a legal principle in tort law that allows a plaintiff to recover damages even if they were partially at fault, provided the defendant had the final opportunity to avoid the accident but failed to do so. This doctrine mitigates the harshness of contributory negligence by shifting the focus to the defendant's ability to prevent the harm.

types.label: New York City Court - Amsterdam
types.definition: New York City Court - Amsterdam is a specific court within the New York City Court system located in Amsterdam, NY.

types.label: JH20 Other Party's expert evidence (UK J-CODE)
types.definition: Considering Other Party(s)' expert evidence, preparing and asking questions of their experts, considering replies, reviewing case in light of such evidence.

types.label: Kansas District Court - Bourbon County
types.definition: A court located in Bourbon County, Kansas that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within its geographical boundaries.

types.label: Georgia Superior Court - Baker County
types.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Baker County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Baker County.

types.label: New Mexico Magistrate Court - Hidalgo County
types.definition: A court located in Hidalgo County, New Mexico that has limited jurisdiction over certain types of cases.

types.label: Missouri Circuit Court - DeKalb County
types.definition: A Missouri Circuit Court in DeKalb County is a specific court within the Missouri Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within DeKalb County.

types.label: Expert Report
types.definition: An Expert Report is a written document that provides an opinion or analysis on a specific subject matter by an individual with specialized knowledge or experience, often used as evidence in legal proceedings.

types.label: Litigation Civil Legal Theories
types.definition: Litigation Civil Legal Theories refer to the various legal arguments and principles that are used in civil litigation cases, such as the doctrine of collateral estoppel or comparative negligence, to support a party's claim or defense.

types.label: Court Reporter
types.definition: Person who provides verbatim recordings of each session of the court and every other proceeding by shorthand, mechanical means, electronic sound recording, or any other method. See 28 U.S. Code § 753

types.label: Procurement Management
types.definition: Procurement Management refers to the process of acquiring goods and services for a business or organization, and involves activities such as identifying needs, selecting vendors, negotiating contracts, and managing supplier relationships.
