types.definition: A Motion to Amend Schedules is a formal request made in bankruptcy proceedings by a debtor seeking to modify previously filed schedules of assets, liabilities, income, expenses, or other financial statements. types.label: Konkani

types.label: Intestinal Failure
types.definition: Intestinal failure is a condition where the intestines are unable to absorb sufficient nutrients and fluids to maintain health, often due to severe functional or structural abnormalities. This condition can result from diseases or surgical interventions that significantly impair the digestive tract's ability to process and absorb essential nutrients, requiring interventions such as total parenteral nutrition (TPN) or enteral nutrition support.

types.label: Waiver and Release Clause
types.definition: A waiver and release clause is a provision in a contract that releases a party from liability for certain actions or events, and waives the right to pursue legal action related to those actions or events.

types.label: E114 Witness fees

types.label: Motion to Determine Final Cure and Mortgage Payment
types.definition: A Motion to Determine Final Cure and Mortgage Payment is a legal request made in a bankruptcy case to determine the final amount needed to pay off a mortgage and bring it current.

types.label: Quasi-Contract Claim
types.definition: A quasi-contract claim is a legal claim that arises when one party receives a benefit from another party, even though there was no actual contract between them, and the law implies a promise to pay for that benefit.

types.label: Quarterly Report
types.definition: A Quarterly Report is a financial report issued by a company every three months to provide an update on its earnings, expenses, and net income. It is required by securities regulators and is aimed at investors and analysts.

types.label: Georgia Superior Court - Bartow County
types.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Bartow County, Georgia, with authority over civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

types.label: M&A G Shareholder / Board Matters Practice
types.definition: A legal practice area that deals with matters related to shareholders and the board of directors in the context of mergers and acquisitions.

types.label: Overtime Violation Claim
types.definition: An overtime violation claim is a legal action initiated by an employee against their employer for not properly compensating them for overtime work. The claim typically arises when an employer does not comply with applicable federal, state, or local overtime laws, which require employers to pay eligible employees at a higher rate for any hours worked beyond a certain number per week or per day. The claim can include allegations of employers failing to pay the required overtime rate, miscalculating the employee's overtime pay, or not properly tracking the employee's overtime hours.

types.label: Estimated, Budgeted, and Actual Engagement Variables

types.label: New Jersey Prerogative Court
types.definition: A New Jersey Prerogative Court is a specialized court within the New Jersey State Courts system that has jurisdiction over appeals of administrative agency decisions.

types.label: Buying Stolen Property

types.label: New Mexico Magistrate Court - Lea County
types.definition: A court located in Lea County, New Mexico that has limited jurisdiction over certain types of cases.

types.label: Due Diligence
types.definition: Due Diligence is the process of conducting a thorough investigation and analysis of a company or business before a merger or acquisition takes place.

types.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Hendricks County
types.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Indiana that hears civil and criminal cases within Hendricks County.

types.label: Venue Clause
types.definition: A Venue Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the location or jurisdiction where any legal disputes arising from the contract will be resolved.

types.label: Mediation Event
types.definition: A Mediation Event is a specific type of Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Event that involves a neutral third party facilitating communication and negotiation between parties in conflict, with the goal of reaching a mutually acceptable resolution.

types.label: Kalmyk; Oirat
types.definition: A language spoken by the Kalmyk people, a Mongolic ethnic group, and the Oirat people, a group of Mongolian and Turkic peoples.

types.label: Waiver of Service of Summons
types.definition: A waiver of service of summons is a legal document that allows a defendant to waive their right to be formally served with a summons and complaint, thereby expediting the legal process.

types.label: L619 Quality assurance and control

types.label: A127 Project Management

types.label: Litigation Finance Management
types.definition: Litigation finance management refers to the process of managing the financial aspects of a legal case, including funding, budgeting, and accounting, in order to maximize the potential return on investment for the parties involved.

types.label: Part-Time Employee
types.definition: A Part-Time Employee is an individual who works fewer hours per week than what is considered full-time by their employer or by labor laws. While part-time employees may have more flexible schedules, they often have limited or no access to benefits like health insurance, retirement plans, and paid time off.

types.label: Arbitration Practice
types.definition: Arbitration, a form of alternative dispute resolution (ADR), is a way to resolve disputes outside the courts. The dispute will be decided by one or more persons (the "arbitrators", "arbiters" or "arbitral tribunal"), which renders the "arbitration award".

types.label: Dissolution for Oppression
types.definition: The concept of "Dissolution for Oppression" refers to a legal claim made by shareholders or partners against a corporation or partnership alleging that the majority shareholders or partners have acted oppressively towards the minority, resulting in the dissolution of the entity.

types.label: Motion for New Trial - Improper Jury Deliberations
types.definition: A Motion for New Trial - Improper Jury Deliberations is a legal request made by a party to a case asking the court to set aside the verdict and order a new trial due to improper conduct during jury deliberations.

types.label: Approval Signatures Clause
types.definition: An Approval Signatures Clause is a provision in a contract that requires the parties to sign and approve the agreement in order for it to be legally binding.

types.label: Bankruptcy and Restructuring Objectives
types.definition: Bankruptcy and Restructuring Objectives refer to the specific aims, goals, plans, and intentions that are constructed by a party in a legal matter related to bankruptcy and restructuring, including the protection of property from damage, rebuttal of presumption of undue hardship, and avoidance action claims.

types.label: Child Dependency Court
types.definition: Child Dependency Court refers to a specialized court that deals with cases involving children who have been removed from their homes due to abuse or neglect, and determines their custody and care arrangements.

types.label: Romany
types.definition: Romany (Language) is a structured system of communication used by the Romani people, consisting of grammar and vocabulary specific to their culture and traditions.

types.label: Originating Country
types.definition: Destination Country, in the context of immigration, refers to the country to which an individual is moving or has moved, with the intention of residing there either temporarily or permanently. The destination country's immigration laws and policies determine eligibility for entry, length of stay, and other rights or obligations.

types.label: Georgia Superior Court - Grady County

types.label: Capitalized Terms Clause
types.definition: A Capitalized Terms Clause is a specific clause within a contract that identifies and defines capitalized terms used throughout the contract.

types.label: Knowledge Management Services
types.definition: Knowledge Management Services refers to professional services that involve the strategic management of an organization's knowledge resources, including the creation, sharing, and utilization of knowledge assets, and are provided by consultants or managers.

types.label: Motion to Certify Appealability
types.definition: A Motion to Certify Appealability is a formal request made to an appellate court to determine whether an appeal can be pursued, typically in cases where the lower court has denied the appeal.

types.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas -  Potter County
types.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Potter County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings at the county level in Pennsylvania.

types.label: Exhaustion of Remedies
types.definition: Exhaustion of remedies refers to the legal principle that a litigant must have pursued and used up all available administrative or legal remedies before seeking judicial review. This requirement ensures that the appropriate administrative or lower court authority has had the opportunity to correct its own errors before higher-level intervention is sought

types.label: New York City Court - Mt. Vernon
types.definition: A court located in Mt. Vernon, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court.

types.label: Workers Compensation Law
types.definition: Law addressing wage replacement and medical benefits to employees injured in the course of employment.

types.label: Homeowners Association Forclosure
types.definition: Homeowners Association Foreclosure is the legal process by which a Homeowners Association (HOA) takes possession of a property within its jurisdiction due to the homeowner's failure to pay association fees or fines. The property is subsequently sold to satisfy the outstanding debt, and the process is governed by state laws and the HOA's governing documents.

types.label: Turnkey Project Clause
types.definition: A turnkey project clause is a provision in a contract that requires the contractor to complete the project and deliver it to the client in a fully operational state, with all necessary components and systems in place.

types.label: Definition of Net Profits Clause
types.definition: A Net Profits Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies how profits will be calculated and distributed among parties involved, after deducting expenses and taxes.

types.label: Management Committee
types.definition: A Management Committee typically oversees the daily operations of an organization, managing broader aspects than those typically handled by an executive committee. This committee is often composed of senior managers across different departments and is responsible for implementing the strategic decisions made by the board or executive committee.

types.label: New York District Court - Nassau County - 3rd District
types.definition: New York District Court - Nassau County (3d Dist.) is a specific court within the New York District Court system, located in Nassau County and designated as the third district.

types.label: Relative Sponsorship Request
types.definition: The Relative Sponsorship Request (in the U.S., I-130 Petition), is the initial step in the process of sponsoring a family member for a family-based immigrant visa (in the U.S., a Green Card). In the United States, the petitioner, typically a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident, files Form I-130 with U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) to establish the qualifying relationship with the intending immigrant relative. Once the I-130 petition is approved, the sponsored relative can proceed with the green card application process, which often involves waiting for a visa number to become available in the appropriate family preference category.

types.label: Customs Recordal Process
types.definition: Customs recordal is a legal mechanism that allows intellectual property rights holders to register their trademarks or other IP rights with customs authorities. This registration enables customs officials to monitor and detain shipments that may contain counterfeit or infringing goods.

types.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Saline County (1st Circuit Court)

types.label: Client Identification Detail
types.definition: Client Identification Detail refers to specific information about a client, such as their organizational unit, business manager, internal counsel, ID, practice group, administrator, tax ID, and name, which is used for invoicing and identifying the legal services buyer.

types.label: Pleadings
types.definition: Pleadings are formal written documents submitted to a court that outline the claims and defenses of parties involved in a legal dispute.

types.label: Pattern or Practice Claim
types.definition: A "Pattern or Practice Claim" refers to a legal claim alleging that a defendant has engaged in a systematic and repeated pattern of discriminatory or unlawful behavior, rather than isolated incidents. This concept is often used in civil rights and employment law cases. In the U.S., these claims are brought under laws like Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, where the claimant must demonstrate that the defendant's actions were not random or isolated but were part of a consistent and regular practice of discrimination or illegal conduct.

types.label: B250 Real Estate

Work of outside vendors, such as private investigators, in assisting the investigation should be an expense under E100. types.label: Alternative Dispute Resolution Management
types.definition: Alternative Dispute Resolution Management refers to the process of resolving legal disputes outside of the traditional court system, such as through mediation or arbitration, and involves managing the various stages of the ADR process.

types.label: Lien Waiver Clause
types.definition: A lien waiver clause is a provision in a contract that requires one party to waive their right to place a lien on the property of another party in exchange for payment or other consideration.

types.label: Tribal Court

types.definition: The AAA Optional Appellate Arbitration Rules are a set of rules created by the American Arbitration Association that parties can choose to use in their arbitration agreement to provide for an optional appeal process.

types.label: Toxic Tort Claims
types.definition: A toxic tort claim arises when an individual alleges harm due to exposure to a toxic substance. This claim seeks compensation for injuries caused by chemicals, pollutants, or other hazardous materials.

types.label: Seat Belt Violation Claim
types.definition: A Seat Belt Violation Claim involves allegations that a driver or passenger has failed to wear a seat belt as required by law, posing a risk to their safety and violating traffic safety regulations.

types.label: Removal of Personal Property Clause
types.definition: A Removal of Personal Property Clause is a provision in a contract that allows one party to take possession of another party's personal property in certain circumstances.

types.label: Resource Management Risk
types.definition: The threats and opportunities associated with the availability and level of resources of an organization to deliver on its mandate, as well as the organization's management of these resources. This risk can arise from an organization's inefficient or ineffective allocation and utilization of its available resources, such as personnel, capital, or physical assets. This can result from poor planning, misaligned priorities, or inadequate controls, potentially leading to operational inefficiencies, increased costs, or unmet objectives, ultimately impacting the organization's overall performance and sustainability

types.label: Negligent Security on Property
types.definition: Negligent Security on Property refers to a legal claim that arises when a property owner fails to provide adequate security measures, resulting in harm or injury to a person on the property.

types.label: Avoidant Personality Disorder

types.label: Motion to Adjourn Settlement Conference

types.label: Pocket Picking Theft
types.definition: The theft of articles from another person’s physical possession by stealth where the victim usually does not become immediately aware of the theft.

types.label: Townhouse
types.definition: A Townhouse is a multi-story residential building that shares one or more walls with adjacent units, featuring individual entrances and often private outdoor spaces such as a patio or garden. Townhouses are typically part of a planned community or row, offering a blend of urban living and private homeownership.

types.label: Failure to Disperse

types.label: Age-Based Market Segment
types.definition: Age-based market segments refer to divisions of the market that are categorized based on the age of consumers. types.label: Paint and Wallpaper Retailers

types.label: A103 Draft/revise

types.label: Indian Child Welfare Act Claim

types.label: Vision Insurance Benefits

types.label: Ownership Clause
types.definition: An Ownership Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies who has the legal right to own and control a particular work product or information.

types.label: Secured Creditor
types.definition: A secured creditor is any creditor or lender associated with an investment in or issuance of a credit product backed by collateral. Secured creditors have a first-order claim on the payouts of a distressed credit investment.

types.label: Critical Care Malpractice
types.definition: Negligence or wrongdoing by a medical professional or facility in the treatment of a critically ill patient, resulting in harm or injury.

types.label: Entry of Default Judgment
types.definition: The Entry of Default Judgment is a legal concept that refers to a court's decision to enter a judgment against a party who has failed to appear or respond to a lawsuit.

types.label: L660 Analysis (NOS)
types.definition: "NOS" = Not Otherwise Specified (catch-all, includes the subcategories). Activities and actions required by litigation teams to be able to make informed decisions about strategy and scope through reliable methods based on verified data. Primarily hourly charges.

types.label: Forcible Entry and Detainer
types.definition: The concept of Forcible Entry and Detainer refers to the illegal act of entering and taking possession of someone else's property without their consent, and the legal actions that can be taken to remove the trespasser and regain possession of the property.

types.label: Restraint of Assets
types.definition: A restraint of assets is a legal concept within matrimonial emergency applications that involves preventing one party from disposing of or transferring their assets in order to preserve them for equitable distribution in a divorce settlement.

types.label: E101 Copying
types.definition: The act of making a reproduction of a document or other material, typically for the purpose of retaining a record or for distribution to others, which is categorized as an expense.

types.label: Financing Practice
types.definition: Agreements to finance a business or other entity.

types.label: Head of State or Government
types.definition: The Head of State or Government is the highest-ranking official in a country, responsible for either ceremonial duties, executive powers, or both, depending on the form of government. In some countries, the roles of Head of State and Head of Government are separate, with the former often being a monarch or president and the latter usually being a prime minister or chancellor.

types.label: TR770 Quasi-Judicial Administrative Proceedings - Domain Names
types.definition: All action associated with completing a quasi-judicial proceeding before an administrative tribunal associated with domain name enforcement actions, including Uniform Domain Name Dispute Resolution (UDRP) actions administered under ICANN and WIPO. Note that governmental fees and external expenses (or "disbursements") are included under E100. This code set is for quasijudicial proceedings only, and any subsequent work completed in a contested matter (i.e. filing complaint or appeal to a national court of jurisdiction) would be expensed under general litigation codes.

types.label: WC380 Alternative Fee Arrangements
types.definition: This code includes all non-hourly or other alternative fee arrangements for tasks and activities in this phase.

types.label: Cargo Claims
types.definition: A cargo claim is a legal action related to the loss or damage of goods during maritime transportation.

types.label: Advance Parole Application
types.definition: The Advance Parole application, commonly submitted on Form I-131 in the United States, allows certain individuals with pending applications for adjustment of status (green card) to travel outside the country and return without abandoning their application. This is particularly important for individuals who have applied for a green card and want to travel before their green card is approved to avoid potential issues with re-entry. Advance Parole is also used by individuals with certain immigration statuses (like DACA recipients) to seek permission to travel internationally while maintaining their legal status

types.label: Invoice Payment Terms
types.definition: Invoice Payment Terms refer to the specific conditions and requirements for payment of a legal fee invoice.

types.label: Modification of Agreement Clause
types.definition: A Modification of Agreement Clause is a provision in a contract that allows the parties to change or amend the terms of the agreement after it has been executed.

types.label: Term Sheet
types.definition: A Term Sheet is a document that outlines the basic terms and conditions under which an investment or significant transaction will be made. It serves as a blueprint for subsequent, more detailed legal agreements. Term Sheets can be binding or non-binding and may include other, significant legal provisions such as non-complete language, no-shop clauses, liquidated damages, etc.

types.label: Burt Lake Band of Ottawa and Chippewa Indians
Liability Clause
types.definition: A Liability Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the responsibility of one party to compensate the other party for any losses or damages incurred as a result of a breach of the contract.

types.label: Right to Sublet Clause
types.definition: The Right to Sublet Clause is a provision in a contract that grants the tenant the legal right to sublet the property to another person for a specified period of time.

types.label: Indiana Circuit Court - Newton County
types.definition: The Indiana Circuit Court - Newton County is a specific court within the Indiana Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Newton County, Indiana.

types.label: Real Estate Commission
types.definition: A real estate commission is a fee paid to real estate agents or brokers for their services in facilitating the sale or purchase of property. It is typically a percentage of the final sale price and compensates the agent for their efforts in marketing, negotiating, and closing the real estate transaction

types.label: Headings Clause
types.definition: A headings clause is a specific type of contractual clause that provides a title or label for each section of a legal document.

types.label: Motion for New Trial - Improper Jury Instructions
types.definition: A Motion for New Trial - Improper Jury Instructions is a legal request made by a party to a case asking the court to set aside the verdict and order a new trial due to errors or mistakes made by the judge in instructing the jury during the trial.

types.label: WC350 Discovery Motions
types.definition: Preparing/responding to/arguing motions that arise from discovery, Review order ruling on motion, Preparing summary of tribunal order

types.label: Circle Up Automation Management
types.definition: Circle Up Automation Management is a concept related to the Legal Point Solutions ontology, which likely refers to the use of automated tools and processes to manage legal tasks and workflows.

types.label: Assignment by Lessor Clause
types.definition: An Assignment by Lessor Clause is a provision in a contract that allows the lessor to transfer their rights and obligations to a third party, typically the lessee, without the need for the lessee's consent.

types.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas -  Butler County
types.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Butler County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in the state of Pennsylvania.

types.label: New York City Court - Utica
types.definition: A court located in Utica, New York that is part of the New York City Court system.

types.label: Rent Implied by Tenant's Occupation
types.definition: A legal concept where a tenant is obligated to pay rent to the landlord, even if there is no written agreement, because the tenant is occupying the landlord's property.

types.label: Savings Account
types.definition: A savings account is a deposit account held at a financial institution that provides a modest interest rate. It is primarily used for the safekeeping of money and often has limitations on the number and types of withdrawals that can be made.

types.label: L100 Case Assessment, Development and Administration
types.definition: L100 Case Assessment, Development and Administration refers to the process of evaluating and managing a legal case, including conducting factual investigations, analyzing legal strategies, managing documents and files, and engaging experts or consultants.

types.label: Child Custody Claim
types.definition: A Child Custody Claim is a legal action brought by a parent seeking to obtain custody of their child, which falls under the broader category of Custody and Visitation Claims.

types.label: Georgia Superior Court - Lincoln County
types.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Lincoln County is a specific court within the Georgia Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases in Lincoln County, Georgia.

types.label: Idea Misappropriation - Contract Claim
types.definition: The wrongful taking or use of another's idea or concept, specifically in the context of a breach of contract claim.

types.label: X123 Publication Costs
types.definition: Any fees associated with publishing an official notice on the matter as required by statute. Excludes electronic or bound resource material purchased for use as a reference (X124) or legal research service costs (X111).

types.label: Writ of Garnishment
types.definition: A Writ of Garnishment is a legal mechanism whereby a court orders a third party to withhold funds they owe to the debtor and to direct the payment to the creditor instead. It's commonly used to collect on a judgment by seizing wages, bank account funds, or other assets that are in the hands of someone other than the debtor.

types.label: Capital Gains
altLabels: Capital Gains refer to the profit realized from the sale or exchange of an asset that has increased in value. This gain is the difference between the purchase price (or basis) of the asset and its selling price, and it is typically subject to taxation.

types.label: Motion Picture and Video Industry
types.definition: The Motion Picture and Video Industry is a branch of the Recording Industry that involves the production and distribution of films and videos for entertainment or educational purposes.

types.label: Clinic Malpractice
types.definition: Clinic Malpractice refers to a type of medical malpractice claim that arises from negligent actions or omissions by healthcare providers in a clinic setting.

types.label: Motion to Compel Supplementation of Excerpts of Record
types.definition: A Motion to Compel Supplementation of Excerpts of Record is a legal request to require additional information to be added to a previously submitted record or evidence.

types.label: Visa for Artist or Entertainer in a Reciprocal Exchange Program
types.definition: This visa (in the U.S., the P-2 visa) is designed for artists or entertainers who will perform as part of a reciprocal exchange program between an organization in the destination country (e.g., U.S.) and an organization in another country. In the United States, the P-2 visa allows for a temporary stay tied to the duration of the specific performance or event, generally for a period of up to one year, with options for extension

types.label: Georgia Superior Court - Evans County
types.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Evans County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Evans County.

types.label: Motor Vehicle Electrical and Electronic Equipment Manufacturing
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing and/or rebuilding electrical and electronic equipment for motor vehicles and internal combustion engines. The products made can be used for all types of transportation equipment (i.e., aircraft, automobiles, trucks, trains, ships) or stationary internal combustion engine applications.

types.label: A112 Billable Travel Time
types.definition: Travel time billed by the timekeeper when other billable services are not performed for the client. Includes time spent waiting for a calendar/court call or other scheduled out-of-office event associated with the matter when other billable services are not performed for the client.

types.label: X101 Copies/Blowbacks/Printing-Black & White (Internal)
types.definition: Any black & white copies, blowbacks, digital prints from images, printing or reprinting costs billed on a per page basis when that printing is performed in-house and not by an external vendor

types.label: Support Activities for Coal Mining
types.definition: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing support activities for coal mining (except geophysical surveying and mapping, site preparation, construction, and transportation activities) on a contract or fee basis. Exploration for coal is included in this industry. Exploration services include traditional prospecting methods, such as taking core samples and making geological observations at prospective sites.

types.label: Telephone Apparatus Manufacturing
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing wire telephone and data communications equipment. These products may be stand-alone or board-level components of a larger system. Examples of products made by these establishments are central office switching equipment, cordless and wire telephones (except cellular), PBX equipment, telephone answering machines, LAN modems, multi-user modems, and other data communications equipment, such as bridges, routers, and gateways.

types.label: Negligent Exposure of Another to Disease or Toxic Substances
types.definition: Negligent Exposure of Another to Disease or Toxic Substances: The failure to exercise reasonable care in preventing the exposure of another person to a disease or toxic substance, resulting in harm or injury to that person.

types.label: inv_start_date
types.definition:
"The starting date for the billing period.  
"

types.label: Month to Month Tenancy Clause
types.definition: A month-to-month tenancy clause is a provision in a contract that allows a tenant to occupy a property on a monthly basis without a fixed term commitment.

types.label: Creditor Matrix
types.definition: A Creditor Matrix or Creditor List is a document that lists the names and addresses of all creditors in a bankruptcy or restructuring case.

types.label: Mixed-Member Majoritarian Representation
types.definition: Mixed-Member Majoritarian Representation (MMM), also known as Parallel Voting, is an electoral system combining first-past-the-post and proportional representation elements, but the two components operate independently. Voters typically have two votes: one for a candidate in a single-member district and another for a party list, with seats filled separately by each method without adjusting for proportionality.

types.label: Utilities Motion
types.definition: A Utilities Motion (Bankruptcy) is a request made by a utility company in a bankruptcy case to receive payment for providing essential services such as electricity, gas, or water to the debtor.

types.label: Author
types.definition: An Author is a specific type of Role in Document or oasis:role that refers to the individual or entity responsible for creating or originating a written work.

types.label: Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity Rights
types.definition: Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity Rights refer to the legal and ethical protections aimed at ensuring individuals are not discriminated against based on their sexual orientation or gender identity. These rights may include freedom from persecution, equal employment opportunities, and access to healthcare and social services, and are increasingly recognized in international human rights law and national legislation.

types.label: Drug Crimes
types.definition: The violation of laws prohibiting the production, distribution, and/or use of certain controlled substances and the equipment or devices utilized in their preparation and/or use.

types.label: Writ of Execution
types.definition: A Writ of Execution is a court order granted to enforce a judgment of possession or to collect on a judgment of monetary damages by allowing the seizure or transfer of the debtor's property by authorities.

types.label: Primary Care Negligence
types.definition: Negligence by a primary care physician in providing medical treatment or advice to a patient, resulting in harm or injury to the patient.

types.label: Impairment of Kidney Function
types.definition: Impairment of kidney function refers to a reduction in the kidneys' ability to filter waste products and excess fluids from the blood. This condition can vary in severity and may lead to chronic kidney disease, necessitating medical management or interventions to prevent further deterioration.

types.label: Trial Court Forum
types.definition: A Trial Court Forum is a level of court forum where legal proceedings are conducted and judgments are made, typically involving the presentation of evidence and witnesses.

types.label: Sac River Band of the Chickamauga - Cherokee
Back Pay
types.definition: Back Pay refers to the wages, benefits, or other forms of compensation owed to an employee for past work performed but not yet paid. This could arise due to miscalculation, wage disputes, legal settlements, or retroactive pay increases.

types.label: Donation
types.definition: A Donation is a voluntary gift of money, goods, services, or property given to an individual, organization, or cause without expectation of reciprocation or direct personal benefit. This act of giving is typically motivated by altruism, support for a specific mission or goal, or a desire to contribute to societal well-being.

types.label: National Upper House Legislator
types.definition: A National Upper House Legislator is a member of the higher chamber in a bicameral national legislature, typically responsible for providing a check on the lower house and representing broader state or regional interests. This official participates in crafting, debating, and voting on national legislation, often with special powers such as confirming executive appointments or ratifying treaties.

types.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas -  York County
types.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - York County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering civil and criminal proceedings at the county level in Pennsylvania.

types.label: Motion to Settle
types.definition: A Motion to Settle is a legal request made by one party to a lawsuit to resolve the case through a mutually agreed upon settlement, rather than proceeding to trial.

types.label: Advertising Law
types.definition: Advertising Law regulates the practices and methods of promoting products, services, and brands to ensure that advertisements are truthful, non-deceptive, and fair. It encompasses regulations on commercial speech, consumer protection, and compliance with industry standards.

types.label: Retention Bonus Clause
types.definition: A retention bonus clause is a provision in a contract that offers an incentive payment to an employee to encourage them to remain with the company for a specified period of time.

types.label: Bankruptcy Schedule - Income
types.definition: Bankruptcy Schedule - Income, also known as Schedule I, requires the debtor to disclose all sources of income, including wages, salaries, business income, rental income, and other earnings. This schedule provides a detailed account of the debtor's financial resources, helping the court and creditors assess the debtor's ability to repay debts.

types.label: Notice and Opportunity to Cure Clause
types.definition: A Notice and Opportunity to Cure Clause is a provision in a contract that requires one party to notify the other party of a breach or default and provide them with a chance to remedy the situation before taking legal action.

types.label: A118 Collection-Forensic
types.definition: For discovery and eDiscovery, the forensic acquisition and analysis of data that includes active files, deleted files and file fragments using specialized software or hardware

types.label: Massachusetts Trial Court - Land Court Department
types.definition: The Massachusetts Trial Court - Land Court Department is a specialized division within the Massachusetts Trial Court that handles cases related to real property disputes.

types.label: Semitic languages
types.definition: Semitic languages are a group of languages that originated in the Middle East and are characterized by a common set of grammatical features and vocabulary.

types.label: Client Relationship Role
types.definition: A lawyer's client relationship role refers to the various capacities in which an attorney interacts with and manages clients on behalf of a law firm. Examples include a billing partner (who oversees billing and invoicing matters), a responsible attorney (who is in charge of managing a specific legal matter), and a relationship attorney (who is in charge of an overall client relationship).

types.label: Motion to Quash Service
types.definition: A Motion to Quash Service is a legal request to invalidate or nullify a summons or other legal notice that was improperly served to a party in a lawsuit.

types.label: UTBMS MF30 Employment, Labor and Employee Benefits
types.definition: A category within the UTBMS coding system used to classify legal services related to employment, labor, and employee benefits, which falls under the broader category of Mergers and Acquisitions.

types.label: Third-Party Summons
types.definition: A third-party summons is a legal document that requires a person who is not a party to a lawsuit to appear in court or provide evidence related to the case.

types.label: Free Cash Flow Conversion Clause
types.definition: A Free Cash Flow Conversion Clause is a provision in a contract that allows for the conversion of a company's free cash flow into equity or debt securities.

types.label: Court Forum
types.definition: A Court Forum is a type of Dispute Forum that is administered by an organization or government entity and has specific levels and jurisdiction types for resolving legal disputes.

types.label: Construction Flooding Negligence
types.definition: The concept of Construction Flooding Negligence refers to a legal claim of negligence against a party involved in construction activities, where the negligence resulted in flooding or water damage to property.

types.label: Employer Breach of Employee Manual
types.definition: The concept of "Employer Breach of Employee Manual" refers to a legal claim made by an employee against their employer for failing to comply with the terms outlined in the company's employee manual.

types.label: Indiana City Court - Hamilton County, Noblesville City
types.definition: Indiana City Court - Hamilton County, Noblesville City is a specific court located in Hamilton County that operates under the jurisdiction of the Indiana City Court, handling cases related to city ordinances and traffic violations.

types.label: Audio and Video Equipment Manufacturing
types.definition: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing electronic audio and video equipment for home entertainment, motor vehicles, and public address and musical instrument amplification. Examples of products made by these establishments are digital video recorders, televisions, stereo equipment, speaker systems, household-type video cameras, jukeboxes, and amplifiers for musical instruments and public address systems.

types.label: Initial Public Offering Practice
types.definition: An Initial Public Offering (IPO) is the process of offering shares of a private company to the public for the first time in order to raise capital, and is a type of Equity Financing.

types.label: Health Care Fraud
types.definition: Health Care Fraud refers to the intentional deception or misrepresentation of information related to health care services or products, with the aim of obtaining unauthorized benefits or payments from a health care program or insurer.

types.label: Architect Malpractice
types.definition: Architect Malpractice refers to a type of malpractice claim that arises from the negligent or wrongful actions of an architect in the design or construction of a building or structure.

types.label: Disclaimer Clause
types.definition: A disclaimer clause is a contractual provision that limits or excludes liability or responsibility for certain risks, damages, or warranties.

types.label: Naturalization Clause Claim
types.definition: A Naturalization Clause claim is a legal assertion related to Article I, Section 8, Clause 4 of the United States Constitution, which grants Congress the power "To establish a uniform Rule of Naturalization." This clause provides the federal government with the authority to set the rules for becoming a U.S. citizen. A claim involving the Naturalization Clause may arise in situations where there is a dispute over the application or interpretation of federal immigration and naturalization laws.

types.label: Definition of Change of Control Clause
types.definition: A Change of Control Clause is a provision in a contract that allows one party to terminate or modify the agreement if the other party undergoes a change in ownership or control.

types.label: B190 Other Contested Matters (excluding assumption/rejection motions)
types.definition: Analysis and preparation of all other motions, opposition to motions and reply memoranda in support of motions

types.label: TR760 Domain Names - ccTLDs Domain Name Filing - Country Code
types.definition: All actions associated with completing a domain name application (including renewal) that is to be filed as a country code top-level domain (ccTLD), e.g., .jp, .uk, .tv. The domain name applications should be filed through the current domain name provider unless otherwise instructed.

types.label: WC330 Depositions
types.definition: Preparing deposition notices and subpoenas, Communicating with witnesses and/or opposing counsel, Discussing deposition strategy with adjuster/employer and/or witness, Preparing witnesses, Reviewing medical records/documents/claims file for deposition preparation, Preparing direct/cross examination questions for depositions, Attending depositions, Travel to and from depositions, Prepare deposition summaries/reports to client

types.label: Florida Circuit Court - Nassau County - 4th Circuit Court
types.definition: A court located in Nassau County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system, which handles civil and criminal cases within its jurisdiction.

types.label: Kansas District Court - Coffey County
types.definition: Kansas District Court - Coffey County refers to a specific court within the Kansas District Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Coffey County.

types.label: Indiana Town Court - Hendricks County, Brownsburg Town
types.definition: A court located in Brownsburg Town, Hendricks County, Indiana that has jurisdiction over local ordinance violations and minor criminal offenses.

types.label: Data Breach
types.definition: A "Data Breach" refers to an incident in which unauthorized individuals gain access to confidential data, often resulting in the exposure or theft of sensitive information. Such breaches can compromise personal, financial, or business-related data, posing risks to individuals, organizations, and stakeholders.

types.label: Abuse of Process
types.definition: The concept of "Abuse of Process" refers to the misuse of legal procedures or the justice system for an ulterior motive, such as to harass or intimidate someone, rather than for the legitimate pursuit of justice.

types.label: Polar Market Segment
types.definition: The Polar Market Segment targets consumers or businesses situated in regions experiencing extremely cold temperatures, such as polar and subpolar zones. Products and services in this segment are designed to address the challenges of living in frigid climates, including insulation, heating solutions, and specialized clothing.

types.label: X202 Patent and Trademark Searching and Monitoring
types.definition: Any searching and monitoring costs, including any monitoring or watch service for a trademark, brand or domain name. Excludes on-line legal research (X111) or discovery/eDiscovery culling and filtering (X302).

types.label: Unit per Task
types.definition: A "Unit per Task" is a type of unit used to measure the cost of a specific task or activity within a legal engagement, such as drafting a contract or attending a hearing.

types.label: Agent Breaching Fiduciary Duty to Principal
types.definition: An agent breaching their legal obligation to act in the best interest of their principal, often an employee breaching their duty to their employer.

types.label: Investors' Rights Agreement
types.definition: An Investors' Rights Agreement (IRA) is a legal document that delineates the rights, privileges, and protections afforded to investors, particularly those investing in private companies. It often includes provisions concerning information rights, anti-dilution protections, and registration rights, among others, aimed at protecting the investors' interests and ensuring they have access to critical information.

types.label: Joint Insurance Agreement
types.definition: A Joint Insurance Agreement allows two or more parties to be jointly insured under one policy. This ensures that all parties have coverage and defines how liabilities or benefits are distributed among them.

types.label: Association
types.definition: An association refers to an organized group of individuals or entities that join together for a common purpose or goal. These groups can take various forms, and they often have specific missions, objectives, and membership requirements. Associations are commonly established to promote shared interests, advocacy, networking, and collaboration among their members.

types.label: Florida Circuit Court - Jackson County - 14th Circuit Court
types.definition: The Florida Circuit Court - Jackson County (14th Circuit Court) is a specific court within the Florida Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Jackson County.

types.label: L652 Objective and Subjective coding
types.definition: Activities and actions related to unitizing and the objective and subjective coding of basic bibliographic information related to both electronic and paper-based data and documents, including auto-coding.

types.label: Georgia Superior Court - Brooks County
types.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Brooks County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Brooks County.

types.label: Lack of Case or Controversy
types.definition: The term "case or controversy" refers to the requirement that courts may only hear matters involving actual, ongoing disputes between parties with a concrete interest in the outcome. This requirement ensures that the judiciary only resolves real conflicts and does not give advisory opinions or engage in issues that are moot, not ripe, or non-justiciable. In the United States, this falls under Article III of the Constitution.

types.label: Trademark Registration Process
types.definition: The Trademark Registration Process involves filing an application with a governmental authority, such as the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), that includes the name, logo, or other mark to be registered, along with the goods or services it will represent. The application undergoes examination for distinctiveness and potential conflicts with existing trademarks; if approved, a Trademark Registration Document is issued, granting the owner exclusive rights to use the mark in commerce for the specified goods or services

types.label: Motions in Appellate Courts
types.definition: Motions in Appellate Courts are requests made by parties in a higher court seeking a specific action or decision, such as a motion to expedite a case or a motion for summary disposition.

types.label: PA220 Patentability Investigation
types.definition: All actions associated with determining the approximate scope of patent protection that may be available for a client's invention, including definition of the scope and field of the search, searching, analysis of search results, and reporting to client. Also known as a "novelty" or "prior art" search, the field of a patentability search is often similar to that of a state-of-the-art search. However, patentability searches are typically conducted after any market research or conceptual engineering has been completed so that the scope of the investigation is described by at least an informal structural or functional description of an invention. Often a patentability search will also locate expired and/or lapsed patents disclosing technology that may be freely copied in order to improve the invention. Thus, a patentability search may include various aspects of a state-of-the-art search. Work of outside vendors in conducting searches or otherwise assisting the investigation should be an expense under E100.

types.label: New York City Court - Cohoes
types.definition: A court located in Cohoes, New York City, which has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical area.

types.label: Deposition Exhibit
types.definition: A deposition exhibit is a physical or digital item presented as evidence during a deposition, which is a pre-trial legal proceeding where witnesses are questioned under oath.

types.label: Washington Superior Court - Asotin County
types.definition: Washington Superior Court - Asotin County refers to a specific court within the Washington Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Asotin County.

types.label: Orthodontics Malpractice
types.definition: Orthodontics Malpractice refers to a type of medical malpractice claim that arises from negligent or improper orthodontic treatment by a healthcare professional.

types.label: B110 Case Administration
types.definition: Coordination and compliance matters, including preparation of statement of financial affairs; schedules; list of contracts; United States Trustee interim statements and operating reports; contacts with the United States Trustee; general creditor inquiries

types.label: tksum segment
types.definition: A "tksum segment" is a component of the LEDES XML E-Billing Ver. 2.2 standard that includes information such as the timekeeper's first and last name, ID, and billing rate.

types.label: Bankruptcy Schedule - Expenses for Separate Household
altLabels: Expenses for Separate Household of Debtor 2 (individuals)
types.definition: Bankruptcy Schedule - Expenses for Separate Household requires the debtor to list the monthly living expenses for a household that is separate from the primary residence, such as an estranged spouse's household or a dependent's separate living arrangement. This schedule details the financial obligations associated with maintaining the separate household, aiding the court and creditors in understanding the full scope of the debtor's financial commitments.

types.label: Skull Valley Band of Goshute Indians of Utah
02 Real Property (PACER NoS)
types.definition: 02 Real Property (PACER NoS) refers to a category of legal cases related to disputes over ownership, use, or transfer of land and buildings, as classified by the PACER Nature of Suit (NoS) Codes.

types.label: Liability to Property Invitees
types.definition: Liability to Property Invitees refers to the legal responsibility of a property owner or occupier to ensure the safety of individuals who are invited onto their property for business purposes, such as customers or clients.

types.label: Motion to Amend Answer
types.definition: A Motion to Amend Answer is a formal request made to the court by a party in a legal case to modify or change their previously filed answer to the complaint or petition.

types.label: Florida County Court - Franklin County
types.definition: Florida County Court - Franklin County is a specific court within the Florida County Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters within Franklin County, Florida.

types.label: Maritime Negligence
types.definition: Maritime Negligence refers to a legal claim for damages resulting from a failure to exercise reasonable care in maritime activities, such as shipping, navigation, or boating.

types.label: Lule Sami
types.definition: Lule Sami is a language within the Language top-level class, spoken by the Lule Sami people in Norway, Sweden, and Finland.

types.label: Minnesota District Court - Carlton County
types.definition: Minnesota District Court - Carlton County: A specific court within the Minnesota District Court system located in Carlton County, responsible for administering legal proceedings within its jurisdiction.

types.label: Debtor in Possession Financing Motion
types.definition: A Debtor in Possession (DIP) Financing Motion is a request made by a bankrupt entity to obtain financing while still in possession of its assets, allowing it to continue operating during the bankruptcy process.

types.label: Contact DBA Name
types.definition: Contact DBA Name refers to the "Doing Business As" name associated with an individual, business, or organization. Unlike the legal name, the DBA name is the alias under which the person or entity operates and may be used in commercial and legal documents to identify the entity.

types.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Randolph County (20th Circuit Court)
Motion to Stay Proceedings Pending Reexamination
types.definition: A Motion to Stay Proceedings Pending Reexamination is a legal request to pause a court case while a reexamination of a patent or trademark is conducted.

types.label: Right to Audit Clause
types.definition: A right to audit clause is a provision in a contract that allows one party to inspect and review the financial records of the other party to ensure compliance with the terms of the agreement.

types.label: Breach of Contract Claims
types.definition: A breach of contract claim is a legal action taken by one party against another for failing to fulfill their obligations as outlined in a contractual agreement.

types.label: Necessity of Trespass
types.definition: The Necessity of Trespass is a legal defense in civil litigation that allows a defendant to justify their trespass onto another's property as necessary to prevent a greater harm.

types.label: Governmental Policy
altLabels: A Governmental Policy is a deliberate plan of action or inaction chosen by a government to address societal issues, guide decision-making, and achieve specific goals. These policies are formulated through legislative, executive, or administrative processes and cover various sectors, including economic, social, environmental, and foreign affairs.

types.label: New Jersey Superior Court - Hudson County
types.definition: The New Jersey Superior Court - Hudson County is a court of general jurisdiction within the New Jersey state court system, located in Hudson County, with authority to hear and decide a wide range of legal disputes.

types.label: New York Supreme Court - Herkimer County
types.definition: The New York Supreme Court - Herkimer County is a court of general jurisdiction in the state of New York that hears civil and criminal cases within Herkimer County.

types.label: Equity Mutual Fund
types.definition: An Equity Mutual Fund is an investment fund that pools capital from multiple investors to buy a diversified portfolio of stocks or equities. The primary objective is to generate high returns through capital appreciation, dividends, or a combination of both, although these funds carry higher volatility and risk compared to debt mutual funds

types.label: Tangible Assets
types.definition: Tangible assets are assets that have a physical existence (we can touch, feel, and see them) except for real estate.

types.label: Mississippi Office of the Attorney General
types.definition: The Mississippi Office of the Attorney General is a government entity responsible for representing the state in legal matters and providing legal advice to state agencies and officials.

types.label: Notice of Judgment
types.definition: A Notice of Judgment is a written notification that officially communicates the decision and outcome of a legal case to the parties involved.

types.label: Matter Percentage Shared Expenses
types.definition: A Matter Percentage Shared Expenses is a type of Engagement Fee Detail that refers to the portion of expenses related to a legal matter that will be shared between the client and the law firm based on a predetermined percentage.

types.label: Top Secret
types.definition: Top Secret is the highest level of classified information, requiring the strictest control and protection due to its potential to cause exceptionally grave damage to national security if disclosed. Access to top secret information is highly restricted and granted only to individuals with the appropriate security clearance and a demonstrated need to know.

types.label: Annual Recurring Revenue
types.definition: Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) is a metric commonly used by subscription-based businesses to measure the total amount of predictable revenue generated from subscriptions over a one-year period. Unlike Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR), ARR provides a longer-term view of revenue stability and is often used for strategic planning and valuation purposes.

types.label: Use Beyond Scope of Permission
types.definition: Use Beyond Scope of Permission refers to a defense strategy in civil litigation where the defendant argues that their actions were not in violation of the law because they were within the scope of their authorized permission.

types.label: Bearer
types.definition: A Bearer in legal contexts refers to an individual or entity responsible for physically transporting or delivering documents, goods, or service of process. This role requires the bearer to ensure the safe and accurate transfer of the item in question, often with a duty to provide confirmation upon successful delivery

types.label: Approval from Prior Employer
types.definition: Approval from a Prior Employer refers to an applicant's receipt of immigration petition approvals from a former employer, applicable to various applications. This approval indicates that the former employer had successfully sponsored the applicant for a specific visa or immigration status.

types.label: Motion to Confirm Termination or Absence of Stay
types.definition: A Motion to Confirm Termination or Absence of Stay is a legal request made in bankruptcy proceedings to confirm that a stay has been terminated or does not exist.

types.label: Document Automation Management
types.definition: Document Automation Management refers to the process of automating the creation, management, and storage of legal documents, specifically within the context of contract and document management.

types.label: Administration of Housing Programs, Urban Planning, and Community Development Industry
types.definition: The Administration of Housing Programs, Urban Planning, and Community Development subsector groups government establishments primarily engaged in the administration of housing, urban planning, and community development.

types.label: Negligent Exercise of Retained Control
types.definition: On a multi-employer work site, a person or entity may be civilly liable if it negligently exercised control so as to have "affirmatively contributed in any way" to the injury.

types.label: Travel Document Issuing Country
types.definition: The Travel Document Issuing Country refers to the country that has issued the travel document or other identification suitable for international travel. This country is usually responsible for the traveler's consular needs and is the authority to which foreign governments will refer for identification and verification purposes

types.label: Implied Indemnification
types.definition: A legal concept where one party is obligated to compensate another party for damages or losses, even if there is no explicit agreement to do so, due to actions or statements that created a reasonable expectation of indemnification.

types.label: Nonacquiescence
types.definition: Nonacquiescence refers to the practice where a government agency chooses not to follow or implement a court ruling that directly affects the agency's actions or policies. This may happen when the agency disagrees with the decision or believes that it only applies to the specific case and not to its general procedures or regulations.

types.label: Contract Duration Clause
types.definition: A Contract Duration Clause is a provision in a contract that specifies the length of time that the contract will remain in effect.

types.label: Obviousness
types.definition: Obviousness in legal terms refers to the lack of novelty and inventiveness in an invention, making it ineligible for a patent. An invention is considered obvious if a person with ordinary skill in the field would find the invention predictable based on prior art.

types.label: Real Estate Investor
types.definition: Entities or individuals that invest in real property, either directly or through a real estate investment trust (REIT).

types.label: Seating Claim
types.definition: A seating claim is a legal action initiated by an employee against their employer for not providing reasonable seating to employees who perform tasks that can be done while seated. The claim typically arises when an employer does not comply with applicable laws, which require employers to provide seating to employees when the nature of their work reasonably permits the use of seats. Employers can face liability for failing to provide seating when required, which can result in physical discomfort or injury to employees who are required to stand for long periods of time.

types.label: Closing Arguments / Summation
types.definition: Closing Arguments/Summation is a trial event where each party presents their final arguments to the jury or judge before a verdict is reached.

types.label: Illinois Circuit Court - Sangamon County (7th Circuit Court)
No Default Clause
types.definition: A "No Default Clause" is a provision in a contract that specifies that neither party can be considered in default unless a specific event or condition occurs, as defined in the contract.

types.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Little River Cty.
types.definition: A court located in Little River County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical area.

types.label: Lawyer
types.definition: A lawyer is a legal professional who provides legal advice and representation to clients in various legal matters, including litigation, transactions, and regulatory compliance.

types.label: Appointment of Successor Trustee Clause
types.definition: An Appointment of Successor Trustee Clause is a provision in a contract that designates a person or entity to take over as trustee in the event that the original trustee is unable or unwilling to continue serving.

types.label: Social Rights
types.definition: Social rights are the rights that focus on ensuring individuals have access to essential social services and protections, such as healthcare, education, and housing. Often considered a subset of economic rights, social rights aim to provide a safety net and foster social cohesion, and they may be protected by international treaties as well as national laws.

types.label: Tax and Revenue Law
types.definition: Law which deals with the constitutional, common-law, statutory, tax treaty, and regulatory rules that constitute the law applicable to taxation.

types.label: Renewable Energy Law Objectives
types.definition: Renewable Energy Law Objectives refer to the legal and regulatory goals aimed at promoting the development, deployment, and integration of renewable energy sources into the energy mix. These objectives address environmental, economic, social, and technological aspects to ensure a transition to sustainable energy systems.

types.label: L632 Scanning - Hard Copy
types.definition: Includes OCR, production of metadata, and other services involved around scanning

types.label: Nephrotic Syndrome
types.definition: Nephrotic Syndrome is a kidney disorder characterized by excessive protein loss in the urine, low blood protein levels, high cholesterol, and swelling (edema). This condition results from damage to the kidney's filtering units (glomeruli) and can lead to complications requiring medical management.

types.label: Misfeasance in Public Office
types.definition: Misfeasance in public office is a legal cause of action in some jurisdictions (e.g., United Kingdom), where a public officer abuses their position by acting unlawfully with malice or reckless disregard for the harm caused. This tort requires proof of deliberate wrongful conduct by the officer, resulting in damage to the claimant.

types.label: Affiliate Non-Debtor
types.definition: An affiliate non-debtor is a company or entity related to a debtor through common ownership, control, or significant financial interest, but which itself is not undergoing bankruptcy proceedings. Such entities may be involved in the bankruptcy case due to financial ties, guarantees, or shared obligations with the debtor.

types.label: Recreational Immunity
types.definition: Recreational immunity exists as a defense for owners and/or occupiers of land as long as the plaintiff's recreational use was uninvited, used without fee, and there was no unreasonable risks that the owner/occupier should have known or knew existed.

types.label: New York City Court - New Rochelle
types.definition: A court located in New Rochelle that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court.

types.label: TR699 Other Trademark Prosecution - International
types.definition: Use only for trademark prosecution activities in connection with applications that are ("international") filed outside the home country or region of the applicant, and that can not be included under a previous code, or as instructed by the client.

types.label: Trial Events
types.definition: Trial Events refer to the specific events that occur during a trial, such as opening statements, witness testimony, and the receipt of a verdict.

types.label: Spousal Support Claim
types.definition: A Spousal Support Claim is a legal request made by one spouse to receive financial assistance from the other spouse following a divorce or separation. This claim is typically based on factors such as income disparity, the length of the marriage, and each spouse's financial needs and contributions during the marriage. Spousal support, also known as alimony, is designed to provide financial support to the lower-earning spouse to help them maintain their standard of living or become financially independent.

types.label: Arkansas Circuit Court - Pike Cty.
types.definition: A court located in Pike County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

types.label: WC410 Fact Witnesses
types.definition: Preparing for examination of witness, Interview/meeting with witness, Preparing for cross-examination of witness, Review & analysis of deposition/trial transcripts

types.label: Respiratory Disorder
types.definition: Respiratory disorders are a group of conditions that affect the respiratory system, including the lungs and airways, leading to symptoms such as difficulty breathing, chronic cough, and reduced oxygen intake. These disorders can range from acute conditions like asthma attacks to chronic diseases like cystic fibrosis, requiring varied treatments and management strategies to improve respiratory function and quality of life.

types.label: Testator
types.definition: A Testator is an individual who creates and executes a valid will, specifying how their estate should be distributed after their death. This person must have the legal capacity to make a will and clearly express their intentions regarding the disposition of their property and assets.

types.label: Delaware Justice of the Peace Court
types.definition: The Delaware Justice of the Peace Court is a court within the Delaware State Courts system that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases involving minor offenses and disputes.

types.label: Personally Identifiable Information
types.definition: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is any data that can be used to identify, contact, or locate a specific individual. This includes names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, social security numbers, and other identifiers that can be linked to a particular person.

types.label: X401 Subscription Fee
types.definition: Delivery of information via a subscription fee as opposed to a per user license fee or on a transaction basis. Indicate # of subscriptions as units; if different rates depending on type of subscription, split into multiple expense lines by rate.

types.label: Trademark Dilution
types.definition: Trademark Dilution is a legal claim that arises when a party uses a similar or identical trademark to another party's famous mark, causing a likelihood of dilution of the distinctive quality of the famous mark.

types.label: Impounding Property to Pay Debt
types.definition: The concept of "Impounding Property to Pay Debt" refers to the legal process of seizing and holding property as collateral to satisfy a debt owed by the property owner, typically in cases of equitable claims.

types.label: Bank Leaving Funds Transfer Incomplete
types.definition: When a bank fails to complete a funds transfer initiated by a customer before the customer closes their account or withdraws their authorization, resulting in the funds not being transferred, and potentially causing financial harm to the customer.

types.label: Promissory Fraud
types.definition: The concept of Promissory Fraud refers to a type of fraudulent misrepresentation where a party makes a promise with no intention of keeping it, in order to induce another party to enter into a contract or take some other action to their detriment.

types.label: Economic Community of West African States
types.definition: ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States): A regional group of fifteen West African countries, founded to promote economic integration across the region.

types.label: Sanctions
types.definition: A penalty or punishment imposed by a court or other authority for a violation of a law or rule, typically involving a fine or other restriction on one's rights or freedoms.

types.label: Certified Rent Roll Clause
types.definition: A Certified Rent Roll Clause is a provision in a contract that requires the landlord to provide a verified list of current tenants and their corresponding rental rates.

types.label: Emergency Medical Treatment and Active Labor Act Claim
types.definition: An EMTALA Claim arises when a healthcare provider fails to comply with the obligations under the Emergency Medical Treatment and Active Labor Act, which requires hospitals to provide emergency medical treatment to all individuals regardless of their ability to pay. This claim involves allegations that the hospital did not provide appropriate medical screening, necessary stabilizing treatment, or an appropriate transfer of an unstable patient.

types.label: Motion to Obtain Oral Argument
types.definition: A Motion to Obtain Oral Argument is a formal request made to a court by a party in a legal case, asking for the opportunity to present their arguments orally before the court.

types.label: Health Law
types.definition: Law, rules, regulations and other jurisprudence among providers, payers and vendors to the health care industry and its patients; and (2) delivery of health care services; all with an emphasis on operations, regulatory and transactional legal issues.

types.label: Arkansas District Court - Polk Cty.
types.definition: A court located in Polk County, Arkansas that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its designated geographic area.

types.label: tax_invoice_cl_id
types.definition: The tax id number for the INVOICE.tax_invoice_cl_name.

types.label: P210 Corporate Review
types.definition: This task includes all fact investigation/due diligence from a corporate perspective, such as structural reviews, material contract reviews, SEC filing reviews, financing document reviews, and industry information reviews.

types.label: Privacy Claims
types.definition: A Privacy Claim is a civil claim that seeks to protect an individual's right to privacy, including claims related to the unauthorized disclosure of personal information, invasion of privacy, and violations of confidentiality by healthcare providers.

types.label: Order of Precedence Clause
types.definition: An Order of Precedence Clause is a provision in a contract that establishes the hierarchy of conflicting terms and conditions within the agreement.

types.label: Key Employee Retention Program Motion
types.definition: A Key Employee Retention Program Motion (KERP) is a request made in a bankruptcy case to retain certain employees who are considered essential to the company's success during the bankruptcy process.
